definition_zh: 灌溉；灌溉系统；所供之水；医学冲洗；河流对土地的补给；灌区；灌溉农业；灌溉工程学
definition_en: the artificial supply of water to land, or the system, water and practice by which this is done
core_image: 干裂的田垄上，一条新挖的沟把河水一点点引到玉米根部，泥土由灰转深
scene: 正午的田埂上，农人提起闸板，让河水顺着沟流进干裂的玉米地。 The farmer lifts the sluice gate and lets river water run down the ditch for irrigation.
sceneCN: 这里 irrigation 指「把水引入农田的行为」（第 1 个义项：人工给土地供水）；句意为农人提起闸板放水，让河水顺着沟流进田里。可辨识物件：田埂、闸板、沟渠、玉米地。

derivatives.zh: 拉丁 irrigare「浇水」的动词形，去掉动作名词后缀 -ation 后得到，语义由「灌溉这一行为」转为「实施灌溉」
基础词 irrigate + -or（拉丁施动者后缀）→ 由「浇水」偏移为「进行灌溉的人或器具」
基础词 irrigate + -able（能力后缀）→ 由「浇水」偏移为「可以灌溉的」
基础词 irrigation + -al（形容词后缀）→ 由「灌溉」偏移为「与灌溉相关的」
micro-（微小）+ irrigation → 由「灌溉」偏移为「微灌，极小尺度的灌溉」
fertilizer 与 irrigation 的混成形式 → 由「灌溉」偏移为「随水施肥」

senses.title: Supply of water to land
senses.definition: the artificial supply of water to fields or crops, usually through channels, pipes or sprinklers
senses.definitionCN: 通过渠道、管道或喷头向农田或作物人工供水
senses.example: Irrigation turned the dry valley into a wheat field.
senses.exampleCN: 灌溉把这条干谷变成了麦田。
senses.why: the noun names the action itself, the plainest sense of the Latin verb irrigare 'to water'.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词直接指行为本身，是拉丁动词 irrigare「浇水」最朴素的义项。

senses.title: System of canals and works
senses.definition: the canals, pipes, pumps and channels built to carry water to land
senses.definitionCN: 为把水送到田间而修建的渠道、管道、水泵与沟渠
senses.example: The irrigation of the plain begins at a stone weir upstream.
senses.exampleCN: 这片平原的灌溉从上游一座石堰开始。
senses.why: once the action is repeated at scale, the word shifts from the act to the built works that make it possible.
senses.whyCN: 当这一行为被大规模重复，这个词就从行为转指使行为得以实现的工程设施。

senses.title: Water delivered
senses.definition: the water that is actually delivered to a field, measured in volume or depth
senses.definitionCN: 实际送到田里的水，按体积或深度计量
senses.example: The irrigation for this plot is measured at the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 这块地的灌水量在闸口处计量。
senses.why: since the verb means to water, the noun can name the water itself rather than the act of giving it.
senses.whyCN: 既然动词意为浇水，名词也可以指水本身，而不指给水这个动作。

senses.title: Washing a wound or cavity
senses.definition: the flushing of a wound, sinus or body cavity with a stream of liquid
senses.definitionCN: 用液流冲洗伤口、窦腔或体腔
senses.example: The nurse recorded the irrigation of the wound in the chart.
senses.exampleCN: 护士把伤口冲洗记录在病历上。
senses.why: medicine borrowed the watering image for washing a body surface with fluid, and the noun followed the verb into that use.
senses.whyCN: 医学借用了「浇水」这一意象，指用液体冲洗体表，名词也随之进入这一用法。

senses.title: Watering by a river
senses.titleCN: 河流对土地的天然补给
senses.definition: the natural watering of land by a river, flood or rising groundwater
senses.definitionCN: 河流、洪水或上升的地下水对土地的自然浸润
senses.example: The annual irrigation of the floodplain keeps its soil fertile.
senses.exampleCN: 洪泛平原每年的自然浸润使土壤保持肥沃。
senses.why: rivers water their banks without any engineer, and the noun extends to that natural supply.
senses.whyCN: 河流无需工程师也会浸润两岸，名词便延伸到这种天然供水。

senses.title: Irrigated land
senses.definition: the tract of land that is supplied with water by a system, considered as a whole
senses.definitionCN: 由灌溉系统供水的一大片土地，作为整体看待
senses.example: The irrigation of the province covers a hundred thousand hectares.
senses.exampleCN: 该省的灌区覆盖十万公顷土地。
senses.why: the noun can stand for the area that receives the water, since the land is what the whole system exists for.
senses.whyCN: 名词可以指接受供水的整片区域，因为整个系统正是为这片土地而存在。

senses.title: Farming that depends on watering
senses.definition: a way of farming in which crops depend on delivered water rather than on rainfall
senses.definitionCN: 作物依赖输送的水而非降雨的耕作方式
senses.example: Irrigation supports two harvests a year in this district.
senses.exampleCN: 灌溉让这个地区一年有两季收成。
senses.why: where rain is unreliable, the practice becomes a whole farming method, and the noun names it.
senses.whyCN: 在雨水不可靠的地方，这种做法成为一整套耕作方式，名词便指这种方式。

senses.title: The engineering field
senses.definition: the branch of engineering and agronomy concerned with designing and managing water delivery
senses.definitionCN: 负责设计与管理输水系统的工程学与农学分支
senses.example: She took a course in irrigation before returning to the family farm.
senses.exampleCN: 她先修了一门灌溉工程课，之后回到家里的农场。
senses.why: a body of technique and theory grows around the practice, and the noun comes to name that field of study.
senses.whyCN: 围绕这一做法生长出一套技术与理论，名词便转而指这个研究领域。

intro.en: Irrigation comes from Latin irrigatio, the noun of action from irrigare 'to water', formed with in- 'into' and rigare 'to moisten'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: irrigation 来自拉丁 irrigatio，是动词 irrigare「浇水」的动作名词，由 in-「进入」与 rigare「润湿」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Rigare meant 'to water, moisten'. Its deeper origin is not established; the links suggested with other watering verbs are hypotheses, so any earlier root offered for it is a reconstructed form.
items.cn: rigare 意为「浇水、润湿」。其更早来源尚无定论；把它与别的「浇水」动词相联系的种种说法都只是假说，因此为它给出的更早词根均属重构形式。

items.en: The prefix in- 'into' combined with rigare to give irrigare 'to lead water into, to water'. The prefix assimilates to ir- before r.
items.cn: 前缀 in-「进入」与 rigare 结合成 irrigare「把水引入、浇水」，前缀在 r 前同化为 ir-。

items.en: Irrigatio was the action noun: the supplying of water, and by extension the works that supplied it.
items.cn: irrigatio 是动作名词，指供水，也引申指供水的设施。

items.en: Medieval Latin kept the word for watering farmland and for washing a body part, and both senses passed into the European languages.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语保留了「浇灌农田」与「冲洗身体部位」两义，二者都传入了欧洲各语言。

items.en: English adopted irrigation in the seventeenth century, first for the watering of land and later for medical flushing.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪吸收了 irrigation，先指给土地浇水，后又指医学冲洗。

items.en: Source uncertain: the origin of rigare is unsettled, and the exact date of its first English use is not recorded, so older forms quoted for it are reconstructed rather than attested.
items.cn: 来源不确定：rigare 的来源无定论，其英语首见的确切年代也无记录，因此为它引用的更早形式属重构形式而非书证。

note.en: Group one separates the word from its close relatives and from the look-alike irritation, which shares sound but not origin; group two separates it from other water words.
note.cn: 第一组把它与近亲词以及形近而不同源的 irritation 分开；第二组把它与别的「水」类词分开。

entries.definition: The verb names the act; irrigation is the noun of action built on it.
entries.definitionCN: 动词指动作；irrigation 是在它之上构成的动作名词。

entries.definition: Describes land or a field that has received water; it modifies the object, not the practice.
entries.definitionCN: 描述已受水的土地或田地；它修饰对象，而不指这种做法。

entries.definition: Says of land that can be irrigated; a capacity word, not the act.
entries.definitionCN: 指土地可以灌溉；这是能力词，不是行为。

entries.definition: From irritare 'to provoke'; it looks and sounds close but has no watering sense at all.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 irritare「激怒」；形音都接近，却与水毫无关系。

entries.definition: The ordinary word for giving plants water; irrigation is the large-scale, engineered version.
entries.definitionCN: 给植物供水的日常说法；irrigation 是大规模、有工程的版本。

entries.definition: The removal of water from land; irrigation brings water in, drainage takes it away.
entries.definitionCN: 把水从土地排走；灌溉送水进来，排水把水带走。

entries.definition: Deliberately covering a field with water, one technique of irrigation rather than its name.
entries.definitionCN: 有意让水淹没田面，是灌溉的一种技术，而不是灌溉本身。

entries.definition: Distributing water in drops; it names one delivery method, while irrigation names the whole practice.
entries.definitionCN: 以水滴形式布水；它指一种输送方式，而 irrigation 指整套做法。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin verb, the built works, real fixed phrases and real derived words.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：拉丁动词、实际工程设施、真实固定搭配与真实派生词。

normal.en: Latin rigare 'to water' plus in- 'into': to lead water into the land.
normal.cn: 拉丁 rigare「浇水」加 in-「进入」：把水引进土地。

normal.en: The family runs irrigate, irrigation, irrigator, irrigable, irrigational.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 irrigate、irrigation、irrigator、irrigable、irrigational。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the practice: irrigation canal, drip irrigation, flood irrigation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出这种做法：灌溉渠、滴灌、漫灌。

normal.en: The tools have their own names: irrigator for the person or device, irrigable for land that can take water.
normal.cn: 工具另有名称：施动者或器具叫 irrigator，能受水的土地叫 irrigable。

normal.en: The opposite word is drainage, which removes the water that irrigation brings in.
normal.cn: 反方向的词是 drainage，它排走灌溉送来的水。

abstract.en: Picture a line drawn in dust with one finger, and water following it to a stalk.
abstract.cn: 想象用手指在尘土里划出一道线，水沿着它流到一株茎前。

abstract.en: Picture a dry field turning dark in bands as each furrow fills.
abstract.cn: 想象干田随着每条沟被灌满，一条条地由灰变深。

abstract.en: Picture a sluice gate lifted by hand, and a whole valley drinking at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手提起闸门，整条山谷同时开始饮水。

examples.en: Ancient irrigation made the first cities possible on land with little rain.
examples.cn: 古老的灌溉让第一批城市得以建在少雨的土地上。

examples.en: The hospital uses irrigation to clean deep wounds before stitching.
examples.cn: 医院在缝合前用冲洗清洁深部伤口。

examples.en: Modern irrigation delivers water drop by drop to save the scarce supply.
examples.cn: 现代灌溉一滴一滴地送水，以节约稀缺的水源。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ir-（进入）+ rig（浇水）+ -ation（名词）」——把水引进田里的这件事 → 灌溉

root: 拉丁 in-「进入」+ rigare「浇水、润湿」→ irrigare「引水入、浇灌」→ irrigatio「供水、灌溉」；rigare 更早来源不确定。英语经法语与晚期拉丁进入。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow the water outward from the act: first the deed and the works, then the water itself, then the borrowed medical wash, then the river's own supply, and finally the land, the farming and the engineering field.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项顺着水从行为向外展开：先是行为与工程，再是水本身，然后是借用的医学冲洗、河流自身的补给，最后是土地、农耕与工程学科。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ditch cut through dry ground, carrying river water to the roots of a crop.
core.cn: 核心意象：在干地上开出一条沟，把河水送到作物的根部。

branches.en: THE ACT AND ITS WATER: the deed of giving water and the water that arrives are named by the same noun.
branches.cn: 行为与其水：给水的动作与到达的水由同一个名词命名。

branches.en: WORKS AND CRAFT: channels and pumps turn the act into an engineered system, and then into a field of study.
branches.cn: 工程与技艺：渠道与水泵把行为变成工程系统，再变成一个研究领域。

branches.en: MEDICAL WASH: a fluid stream cleans a wound or cavity, borrowing the watering image.
branches.cn: 医学冲洗：液流清洁伤口或体腔，借用了浇水的意象。

branches.en: RIVER SUPPLY: a river waters its floodplain with no machinery at all.
branches.cn: 河流补给：河流无需任何机械便浸润自己的洪泛平原。

branches.en: LAND AND FARMING: the watered tract, and the farming method that depends on delivered water.
branches.cn: 土地与农耕：受水的那片地，以及依赖输水的耕作方式。

intro.en: Irrigation can be read in parts: an assimilated Latin prefix, a Latin verb of watering, and an action-noun suffix.
intro.cn: irrigation 可按部分读出：一个同化的拉丁前缀、一个表示浇水的拉丁动词，以及一个动作名词后缀。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is genuine here: irrigare, irrigatio, irrigator and irrigabilis all belong to the same verb, and rigare is the watering root behind them.
latinIntro.cn: 这里的拉丁词族是真实的：irrigare、irrigatio、irrigator 与 irrigabilis 都属同一个动词，rigare 是它们背后的浇水词根。

items.structure: Latin in- 'into', assimilated to ir- before r
items.example: The prefix directs the water inward to the field.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把水引向田里。

items.example: The root appears again in irrigate and irrigator.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根也出现在 irrigate 与 irrigator 中。

items.structure: Latin -atus, past participle and verb ending
items.example: Irrigate is the verb built on the root.
items.exampleCN: irrigate 是在这个词根上构成的动词。

items.example: Irrigation names the act and its result.
Farmers irrigate the fields in spring.

items.meaning: one who or that which irrigates
items.example: The irrigator checks the gate each morning.
items.exampleCN: 灌溉者每天早上检查闸口。

items.example: The lower field is irrigable; the ridge is not.
items.exampleCN: 低处的田可以灌溉，山脊则不行。

items.example: Irrigational works changed the valley.
items.exampleCN: 灌溉工程改变了这条山谷。

items.meaning: watering on a very small scale
items.example: Microirrigation saves water in orchards.
Fertigation delivers nutrients with the drip line.
items.exampleCN: 水肥一体化让养分随滴灌管送达。

latinEntries.meaning: a watering, a supplying of water

definition_zh: 核聚变；轻原子核结合成较重原子核并释放能量的过程
definition_en: the process in which two light atomic nuclei join to form a heavier nucleus, releasing energy
core_image: 两粒很小的核被极高的热逼到一起，合为一粒更大的核，同时放出一束光
scene: 太阳核心把氢变成氦，光与热就这样产生。 Nuclear fusion in the sun's core turns hydrogen into helium.
sceneCN: 这里 nuclear fusion 指「轻核结合成较重核并释放能量」（第 1 个义项：轻原子核合并的核反应过程）；句意：太阳核心的核聚变把氢变成氦。图中可辨识物件：太阳剖面、核心区、氢核、氦核。

senses.title: Light nuclei joining into a heavier one
senses.definition: the nuclear reaction in which two light nuclei combine to form a heavier nucleus
senses.definitionCN: 两个轻原子核结合成一个较重原子核的核反应
senses.example: Deuterium and tritium are the easiest fuels for nuclear fusion.
senses.exampleCN: 氘与氚是核聚变最容易使用的燃料。
senses.why: Latin fusion means 'a pouring together', and the two nuclei are literally poured into one larger body.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语本义是「倒在一起」，两粒核确实被倒进一个更大的身体里。

senses.title: The power source of stars
senses.definition: the fusion reactions in stellar cores that keep stars shining for billions of years
senses.definitionCN: 恒星核心中使恒星发光数十亿年的聚变反应
senses.example: Without nuclear fusion the sun would collapse within hours.
senses.exampleCN: 没有核聚变，太阳会在数小时内坍缩。
senses.why: Gravity squeezes the core until hydrogen nuclei merge, and the released energy balances the squeeze.
senses.whyCN: 引力把核心压到氢核合并，放出的能量又抵住这份挤压。

senses.title: The laboratory attempt to hold a plasma
senses.titleCN: 实验室里约束等离子体的尝试
senses.definition: research that confines a hot ionized gas long enough for fusion to occur
senses.definitionCN: 把高温电离气体约束足够久、使聚变得以发生的研究
senses.example: Magnetic fields are used to keep the plasma away from the walls.
senses.exampleCN: 磁场被用来让等离子体远离器壁。
senses.why: Fusion needs temperatures above the sun's core, so the central problem is containment rather than fuel.
senses.whyCN: 聚变需要高于太阳核心的温度，因此核心难题是约束，而不是燃料。

senses.title: The fusion power plant
senses.definition: an engineered reactor designed to produce useful heat from fusion, such as a tokamak
senses.definitionCN: 为从聚变获得可用热量而设计的工程反应堆，如托卡马克
senses.example: The tokamak is the most developed nuclear fusion design.
senses.exampleCN: 托卡马克是最成熟的核聚变设计。
senses.why: Once the physics is understood, the phrase names the machine that would turn it into power.
senses.whyCN: 物理被理解之后，这个短语便指那台将把它变成电力的机器。

senses.title: The thermonuclear weapon
senses.definition: an uncontrolled fusion reaction ignited by a fission explosion
senses.definitionCN: 由裂变爆炸点燃的不受控聚变反应
senses.example: A hydrogen bomb relies on nuclear fusion for most of its yield.
senses.exampleCN: 氢弹的大部分当量来自核聚变。
senses.why: Fusion releases far more energy per unit mass, so weapons use it as a second, larger stage.
senses.whyCN: 聚变每单位质量放出的能量多得多，因此武器把它用作更大的一级。

senses.title: Net energy gain
senses.definition: the condition in which a fusion reaction returns more energy than was spent heating and confining it
senses.definitionCN: 聚变反应放出的能量超过用于加热与约束的能量
senses.example: The experiment finally reached net energy gain from nuclear fusion.
senses.exampleCN: 这次实验终于实现了核聚变的净能量增益。
senses.why: A power source is only useful if it pays back its own running cost, so breaking even became a milestone with its own phrase.
senses.whyCN: 一种能源只有偿还自身运行成本才有用，因此「收支相抵」成了有专门说法的一座里程碑。

senses.title: The disputed tabletop claim
senses.titleCN: 有争议的台面聚变说法
senses.definition: the 1989 claim that fusion could occur in simple room-temperature cells, which was not reproduced
senses.definitionCN: 1989 年声称聚变可在简单的室温装置中发生，但未能被重复
senses.example: Cold fusion was announced as nuclear fusion at room temperature.
senses.exampleCN: 「冷聚变」曾被宣布为室温下的核聚变。
senses.why: The claim borrowed the prestige of fusion while skipping the extreme conditions, which is why the term still carries doubt.
senses.whyCN: 这一说法借用了聚变的声望，却跳过了极端条件，因此该术语至今带着疑问。

senses.title: The helium ash that must be removed
senses.definition: the helium produced by fusion, which must be exhausted so that it does not dilute the fuel
senses.definitionCN: 聚变产生的氦，必须排出，以免稀释燃料
senses.example: The reactor must pump out the helium ash from nuclear fusion.
senses.exampleCN: 反应堆必须把核聚变产生的氦灰抽走。
senses.why: A furnace that keeps its own ashes will smother, so the product of fusion becomes an engineering problem with a name.
senses.whyCN: 留着自身灰烬的炉子会闷灭，因此聚变的产物成了一个有名字的工程问题。

intro.en: Nuclear fusion joins the Latin kernel word to Latin fusio 'a pouring', from fundere 'to pour, to melt'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: nuclear fusion 把拉丁语的「果仁」接到拉丁 fusio「倾倒」上，而 fusio 出自 fundere「倒、熔」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Fundere meant 'to pour, to melt, to cast', and it produced the image of separate things flowing into one.
items.cn: fundere 意为「倒、熔、铸」，造出了分开之物流成一体的意象。

items.en: Fusio named a pouring or a melting, the act that turns separate pieces into a single mass.
items.cn: fusio 指倾倒或熔合，是把分开的块变成一整团的动作。

items.en: English borrowed fusion for melting and for the joining of things, long before it meant a nuclear reaction.
items.cn: 英语借入 fusion 指熔化与结合，远在它指核反应之前。

items.en: Twentieth-century physics explained starlight as the fusion of hydrogen into helium, and the word moved to the nucleus.
items.cn: 二十世纪物理学把星光解释为氢聚变成氦，这个词于是移到了原子核上。

items.en: Controlled fusion research added fusion reactor, plasma confinement and net gain to the vocabulary.
items.cn: 受控聚变研究又为词汇添了聚变堆、等离子体约束与净增益。

items.en: The first uses of the exact phrase are approximate; the Latin chain is fully recorded.
items.cn: 这个确切短语最早的使用年代为约数；拉丁语链条有完整记录。

note.en: Group one holds pour-root look-alikes and one near-twin from a splitting root; group two holds words for joining and for the rival reaction.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「倾倒」词根的形近词，外加一个来自「分裂」词根的近形词；第二组是表示结合与竞争反应的说法。

entries.definition: The general word for melting or joining, also used of cuisine and music; the nuclear phrase narrows it to nuclei.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指熔化或结合，也用于烹饪与音乐；核短语把它收窄到原子核。

entries.definition: To melt together, or the safety device that melts to break a circuit; both keep the pouring-and-melting image.
entries.definitionCN: 熔合，或熔断以断开电路的安全装置；两者都保留「倾倒与熔化」的意象。

entries.definition: From Latin findere 'to split': a crack or a cleft, close in shape to fusion but opposite in image.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁语「分裂」：指裂缝或裂口，形状接近但意象相反。

entries.definition: Latin con- 'together' plus fundere 'pour': to pour things together until they cannot be told apart.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁「共同」加「倒」：把东西倒在一起，直到分不清。

entries.definition: The splitting of a heavy nucleus; it releases energy in the opposite direction from fusion.
entries.definitionCN: 重核裂开；它从相反方向释放能量，与聚变相对。

entries.definition: Describing fusion driven by very high temperature, as in stars and hydrogen bombs.
entries.definitionCN: 描述由极高温驱动的聚变，如恒星与氢弹中的情形。

entries.definition: The general word for two bodies becoming one; it carries no nuclear meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指两个实体合而为一；不含核物理含义。

entries.definition: Greek 'a putting together': the building of a whole from parts, often chemical rather than nuclear.
entries.definitionCN: 希腊语「放在一起」：由部分组成整体，常指化学而非核过程。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin nucleus 'kernel' plus fusio 'a pouring': two kernels poured into one.
normal.cn: 拉丁「果仁」加「倾倒」：两粒仁被倒成一粒。

normal.en: The family runs nuclear fusion, fusion, fusion reactor, thermonuclear.
normal.cn: 同族表达包括核聚变、聚变、聚变堆、热核的。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: controlled nuclear fusion, nuclear fusion research, nuclear fusion power.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：受控核聚变、核聚变研究、聚变能。

normal.en: Fusion and fission are opposites: one pours together, the other splits apart.
normal.cn: 聚变与裂变相反：一个倒在一起，一个裂开。

normal.en: The sun is the oldest working fusion reactor, and it needs no containment.
normal.cn: 太阳是最古老的运转中的聚变堆，而且不需要约束装置。

abstract.en: Picture two small flames pressed into one larger flame.
abstract.cn: 想象两簇小火被压成一簇更大的火。

abstract.en: Picture a furnace that must also sweep away its own ashes.
abstract.cn: 想象一座还得扫掉自身灰烬的炉子。

abstract.en: Picture a star held up by the very fire it is making.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗恒星被自己造出的火撑住。

examples.en: Nuclear fusion requires temperatures of millions of degrees.
examples.cn: 核聚变需要数百万度的温度。

examples.en: The sun's nuclear fusion has run for billions of years.
examples.cn: 太阳的核聚变已经运行了数十亿年。

examples.en: Engineers still cannot sustain nuclear fusion for long periods.
examples.cn: 工程师仍无法长时间维持核聚变。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「nuclear（核的）+ fusion（融合）」——核与核融在一起，就是核聚变

root: nuclear（拉丁 nucleus「果仁、核」）+ fusion（拉丁 fusio「倾倒」← fundere「倒、熔」）。英语 nuclear fusion。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow two nuclei joining: the reaction, the star, the laboratory plasma, the power plant, the weapon, net gain, the disputed cold claim and the helium ash left behind.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着两粒核的结合展开：反应本身、恒星、实验室等离子体、发电装置、武器、净增益、有争议的冷聚变说法，以及留下的氦灰。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two tiny kernels forced together by heat, becoming one larger kernel and releasing a flash.
core.cn: 核心意象：两粒小核被热逼到一起，合成一粒更大的核，并放出一道闪光。

branches.en: THE REACTION: the laboratory description and the stellar furnace are the same joining at two scales.
branches.cn: 反应：实验室的描述与恒星熔炉，是同一结合的两个尺度。

branches.en: THE CONTAINMENT: research holds a plasma, and engineering designs the reactor around that hold.
branches.cn: 约束：研究把等离子体困住，工程则围绕这个「困住」设计反应堆。

branches.en: THE EXTREMES: released at once it is a weapon, released profitably it must return more than it costs.
branches.cn: 两个极端：一次性释放是武器，要有利可图则须产出大于投入。

branches.en: THE SHORT CUT: a claim tried to skip the heat, and the doubt is part of the word's history.
branches.cn: 捷径：有人试图跳过高温，疑问于是成了这个词历史的一部分。

branches.en: THE RESIDUE: the helium produced must be swept out or the fire smothers.
branches.cn: 残余：产生的氦必须扫出去，否则火会闷灭。

intro.en: The phrase joins the Latin kernel word to a Latin noun of pouring, so both halves describe the same act of merging.
intro.cn: 这个短语把拉丁语的「果仁」接到拉丁语的「倾倒」名词上，两半都在描述同一个合并动作。

latinIntro.en: Latin fundere and fusio also yield fuse, fusion, confuse and refuse; Latin nucleus yields nuclear and nucleic.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 fundere 与 fusio 还衍生出 fuse、fusion、confuse、refuse；拉丁 nucleus 衍生 nuclear 与 nucleic。

items.example: The nucleus supplies the fuel.
The verb describes separate pieces flowing into one.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词描述分开的块流成一体。

items.example: The noun names the act of merging.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指合并的动作。

items.example: The fusion of two companies created one firm.
items.exampleCN: 两家公司的合并造出一家公司。

items.example: Nuclear fusion powers the stars.
The fusion reactor held the plasma for seconds.
items.exampleCN: 聚变堆把等离子体约束了几秒。

items.example: The thermonuclear explosion was detected at once.
items.exampleCN: 热核爆炸立刻被探测到。

items.example: The two wires fused in the heat.
items.exampleCN: 两根导线在高温中熔在一起。

senses.why: The regular space allowed personal comment.

definition_zh: 离散的；分开的；独立的；不连续的；分段式的
definition_en: separate and distinct, existing as individual units rather than as one continuous whole
core_image: 实验台上摆着一排互不相连的方块灯，每两盏之间留着一指宽的暗缝，各自有独立的开关
scene: 实验台上摆着一排互不相连的方块灯，每两盏之间留出一道暗缝，每盏灯都有自己的开关。 Each reading comes from a discrete sensor with its own wire.
sceneCN: 这里指彼此分开、各自独立的单元（第 1 个义项：分离独立）；句意为每个读数都来自一个自带线路的独立传感器。图中可辨识物件：方块灯、暗缝、独立开关。

derivatives.zh: 由该形容词加副词尾构成，义为「分开地；离散地」
由该形容词加表示性质的名词尾构成，义为「离散性；分离性」
由该形容词加动词尾构成，义为「使离散化；离散处理」
由离散化动词加名词尾构成，义为「离散化」
由否定前缀加该形容词构成，义为「未分开的；不分明的」

senses.title: Separate and distinct
senses.definition: existing as a separate unit that is clearly apart from others and not merged with them
senses.definitionCN: 作为与其他事物明显分开、不被合并的独立单元存在
senses.example: The two faults are discrete and need separate repairs.
senses.exampleCN: 这两处故障彼此独立，需要分别修理。
senses.why: Latin discretus meant separated or distinguished, and this plain sense of standing apart is the base of every later use; the same participle also produced the homophone discreet, the word for cautious behaviour.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语「discretus」意为分开的或辨别出来的，这种「各自分开」的本义是后来一切用法的根基；同一个分词还产生了同音词「discreet」，即言行谨慎之义。

senses.title: Taking separate values
senses.definition: changing only in separate countable values rather than over a smooth and unbroken range
senses.definitionCN: 只在可数的分离数值之间变化，而不是在平滑连续的区间上变化
senses.example: A discrete variable can take only whole numbers.
senses.exampleCN: 离散变量只能取整数。
senses.why: Mathematics took the word's core idea of separate units and applied it to quantities that jump from one value to the next.
senses.whyCN: 数学借用了这个词「分离单元」的核心意思，用来指从一个数值跳到下一个数值的量。

senses.title: Data kept as separate items
senses.titleCN: 以分离条目保存的数据
senses.definition: stored as individual records or categories rather than as one continuous stream
senses.definitionCN: 以一条条独立记录或类别保存，而不是作为一条连续的数据流
senses.example: The survey collects discrete data on each household.
senses.exampleCN: 这项调查收集每户的离散数据。
senses.why: Once values are counted separately, the records themselves are called discrete, and computing made this sense common.
senses.whyCN: 数值一旦被分开计数，记录本身也就被称为离散的，计算机领域使这一义项流行起来。

senses.title: Divided into separate stages
senses.definition: broken into separate parts or stages with clear gaps between them
senses.definitionCN: 被切分为彼此有明显间隔的部分或阶段
senses.example: The training runs in discrete stages of four weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 培训分为每期四周的独立阶段。
senses.why: A process cut at fixed points looks like a row of separate blocks, so the word also describes anything divided into stages.
senses.whyCN: 过程在固定节点被切开，看起来就像一排分开的块，因此这个词也形容被分成阶段的事物。

senses.title: Individual and particular
senses.definition: considered one by one as a particular case, apart from the rest of its class
senses.definitionCN: 作为特定个案逐个考虑，与其同类中的其余部分分开
senses.example: Each discrete case was reviewed by a different judge.
senses.exampleCN: 每个单独的案例都由不同的法官审理。
senses.why: If units are separate, attention can fall on one alone; this sense stresses the single item rather than the gap between items, while discreet still keeps its own meaning of caution.
senses.whyCN: 单元既然分开，注意力就可以只落在一个上面；这个义项强调单个个体，而不是个体之间的间隔，而「discreet」仍保留谨慎这一独立含义。

senses.title: A signal defined at separate instants
senses.titleCN: 在分离时刻取值的信号
senses.definition: a signal whose value is defined only at separate moments, as in digital or sampled systems
senses.definitionCN: 只在分离时刻才有确定取值的信号，如数字系统或采样系统中的信号
senses.example: The receiver converts the wave into a discrete signal.
senses.exampleCN: 接收机把波转换成离散信号。
senses.why: Electronics borrowed the mathematical sense: a sampled wave exists as a series of separate points, not as a smooth line.
senses.whyCN: 电子学借用了数学义：采样后的波是一串分离的点，而不是一条平滑的线。

senses.title: An isolated group of one species
senses.definition: a group of organisms of one species that is separated from other groups and breeds mainly within itself
senses.definitionCN: 同一物种中与其他群体隔开、主要在群体内部繁殖的一群生物
senses.example: The valley holds a discrete population of frogs.
senses.exampleCN: 这条山谷里有一个分离的蛙类种群。
senses.why: Ecology reused the notion of a bounded unit: a population with a clear edge is separate from its neighbours.
senses.whyCN: 生态学沿用了「有边界的单元」这一概念：边界清楚的种群与邻近种群分开。

senses.title: A model that jumps between events
senses.definition: a computer model in which the state changes only at separate scheduled events rather than continuously
senses.definitionCN: 一种计算机模型，其状态只在分离的预定事件发生时改变，而不是连续变化
senses.example: The airport model is a discrete simulation of gate use.
senses.exampleCN: 这个机场模型是对登机口使用情况的离散模拟。
senses.why: Simulation inherited the word from mathematics and computing, because the model steps from one event to the next.
senses.whyCN: 模拟技术从数学与计算领域继承了这个词，因为模型是从一个事件跳到下一个事件。

intro.en: Discrete comes from Latin discretus, the past participle of discernere, to separate or distinguish, formed from dis-, apart, and cernere, to sift. The same participle also produced discreet, the word for cautious behaviour, so the two English adjectives are homophones with different meanings.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语「discretus」，是动词「discernere」（分开、辨别）的过去分词，由「dis-」（分开）加「cernere」（筛、辨别）构成。同一个分词也演化出表示言行谨慎的「discreet」，因此这两个英语形容词同音而异义。

items.en: The prefix meant apart or away, and it marks the act of putting things at a distance from one another.
items.cn: 这个前缀表示分开、离开，标记把事物彼此拉开距离的动作。

items.en: The verb meant to sift, to separate and to distinguish, the image behind a sieve or a screen.
items.cn: 这个动词意为筛、分开、辨别，其意象来自筛子或筛网。

items.en: With the prefix added, the verb meant to separate apart and hence to tell one thing from another.
items.cn: 加上前缀之后，这个动词意为分开，进而指把一事物与另一事物辨别开来。

items.en: The past participle meant separated or distinguished, and it became the direct source of the English adjective.
items.cn: 这个过去分词意为被分开的或被辨别出的，后来成为这个英语形容词的直接来源。

items.en: English adopted the form for things that stand apart, especially in mathematics and later in computing.
items.cn: 英语采用这一形式表示彼此分开的事物，尤见于数学，后来又用于计算领域。

items.en: The same Latin participle also gave English discreet, meaning careful in speech or behaviour; the two words sound alike but must not be confused.
items.cn: 同一个拉丁分词还给了英语「discreet」，意为言行谨慎；两个词读音相同，但不可混淆。

note.en: The first group gathers forms that look or sound like discrete; the second group gathers words for separation and difference.
note.cn: 第一组收录在形音上与「discrete」相近的形式；第二组收录表示分开与差异的说法。

entries.definition: Careful and prudent in speech or behaviour; it sounds the same as discrete but belongs to a different sense of the same Latin participle.
entries.definitionCN: 指说话或举止谨慎小心；与「discrete」读音相同，但属于同一拉丁分词的另一义。

entries.definition: In a careful and prudent manner, with no relation to separate units.
entries.definitionCN: 指以谨慎小心的方式，与「分离的单元」无关。

entries.definition: The freedom or power to decide, and the quality of being careful about what one says.
entries.definitionCN: 指决定权或裁量权，也指说话谨慎的品质。

entries.definition: To perceive or distinguish something that is not obvious.
entries.definitionCN: 指察觉或辨别不明显的事物。

entries.definition: A difference between two things that should agree; it looks close but comes from another Latin verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指本应一致的两事物之间的差异；形近但来自另一个拉丁动词。

entries.definition: Apart from others, not joined or shared.
entries.definitionCN: 指与他人分开、不连接或不共有的。

entries.definition: Clearly different and easily told apart from something else.
entries.definitionCN: 指明显不同、容易与其他事物区分开的。

entries.definition: Single and considered on its own, apart from the group.
entries.definitionCN: 指单个的、单独看待而不计入群体的。

entries.definition: Broken off and not continuing without a gap.
entries.definitionCN: 指中断的、不能无间隔延续的。

entries.definition: Separated from something it was once connected to.
entries.definitionCN: 指与原先把连在一起的事物分开的。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the Latin sieve behind the word, the real spelling contrast with discreet, and the real technical phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用这个词背后的拉丁筛子、与「discreet」的真实拼写差别，以及真实的技术搭配。

normal.en: Cernere is to sift: discrete things have already been sifted apart.
normal.cn: 「cernere」是筛，离散的事物已经被筛分开。

normal.en: In discrete the two e letters are separated by t, which is exactly what the word means.
normal.cn: 「discrete」里的两个「e」被「t」隔开，正好就是这个词的意思。

normal.en: In discreet the two e letters sit together, a neat sign that the word is not about separation.
normal.cn: 「discreet」里的两个「e」挨在一起，正好提示这个词与分离无关。

normal.en: Discrete data, discrete points and discrete steps are ordinary terms in statistics and computing.
normal.cn: 离散数据、离散点与离散步骤是统计与计算领域的常用说法。

normal.en: A discrete event happens at one scheduled moment, so the model jumps from event to event.
normal.cn: 离散事件在某个预定时刻发生，因此模型从一个事件跳到下一个事件。

abstract.en: A discrete thing is a bead on a string: the string is continuous, the beads are not.
abstract.cn: 离散之物像线上的珠子：线是连续的，珠子不是。

abstract.en: Separateness can be a virtue: clear units are easier to count, store and compare.
abstract.cn: 分开也可以是一种优点：清楚的单元更容易计数、保存与比较。

abstract.en: The quiet danger is the homophone: the careful adviser is discreet, the separate unit is discrete.
abstract.cn: 无声的危险在同音：谨慎的顾问是「discreet」，分开的单元是「discrete」。

examples.en: The samples fall into three discrete groups.
examples.cn: 样本分成三个彼此独立的组。

examples.en: She keeps her work and home life discrete.
examples.cn: 她把工作与家庭生活分开。

examples.en: The software records each keystroke as a discrete event.
examples.cn: 该软件把每次按键记录为一个离散事件。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「迪斯克瑞特」——两段彼此断开叫分开，信号只在点上取值叫离散：分开、离散

root: 拉丁语「discretus」←「discernere」「分开、辨别」←「dis-」「分开」+「cernere」「筛、辨别」；同一个分词又演化出「discreet」「谨慎的」，二者同音异义，具体派生年代各家标注不一。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from simple separation to technical modelling: separate units, mathematical values, stored data, broken stages, individual cases, sampled signals, isolated populations, and event-driven simulation.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从简单分开走向技术建模：分离的单元、数学取值、存储数据、分段阶段、个别案例、采样信号、隔离种群、事件驱动模拟。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of lamps stands apart, each with its own switch and its own dark gap.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排灯各自独立，每盏都有自己的开关与暗缝。

branches.en: THE SEPARATE ITEM: one unit stands apart, and attention can rest on that single case.
branches.cn: 分开的个体：一个单元独立存在，注意力也可以落在这单个案例上。

branches.en: THE COUNTED VALUE: numbers and records exist as separate points rather than a smooth range.
branches.cn: 计数的值：数值与记录以分离的点存在，而不是平滑区间。

branches.en: THE CUT PROCESS: a whole is divided into stages with clear gaps between them.
branches.cn: 切分的过程：整体被分成有明显间隔的阶段。

branches.en: THE SAMPLED WAVE: a signal lives only at separate instants in a digital system.
branches.cn: 采样的波：信号在数字系统中只存在于分离的时刻。

branches.en: THE BOUNDED MODEL: an isolated population and a simulation that steps from event to event.
branches.cn: 有边界的模型：隔离的种群，以及逐个事件推进的模拟。

intro.en: Discrete is the adjective of a Latin verb of separating, and its family includes both the technical words and the dangerous homophone.
intro.cn: 这个形容词出自一个表示分开的拉丁动词，其词族既包括技术词，也包括那个危险的同音词。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies cernere, discernere and the participle discretus; the last form is the immediate source of the English adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了「cernere」、「discernere」与分词「discretus」；最后一个形式是这个英语形容词的直接来源。

items.example: The prefix pulls the two units apart.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把两个单元拉开。

items.meaning: to sift, to separate, to distinguish
items.example: The sieve image sits at the centre of the family.
items.exampleCN: 筛子的意象处在这个词族的中心。

items.structure: Latin verb from dis- and cernere
items.example: The verb names the act of telling things apart.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词指把事物辨别开来的动作。

items.example: The participle became the English adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词变成了这个英语形容词。

items.example: The ending marks a completed act.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾标记已完成的动作。

items.example: English kept the meaning of standing apart.
items.exampleCN: 英语保留了「彼此分开」的意思。

items.structure: English adjective from the same participle
items.example: The same source split into two English words.
items.exampleCN: 同一来源分成了两个英语词。

items.meaning: the power to decide; cautious judgement
items.example: The noun belongs with the cautious branch.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词属于「谨慎」那一支。

items.structure: English adjective with a negative prefix
items.example: The negation returns to the literal idea of separation.
items.exampleCN: 否定前缀回到字面上的「分开」之意。

definition_zh: 经济收缩；产出与就业下降的阶段
definition_en: a period in which an economy's output, employment and spending are shrinking
core_image: 集装箱堆到三层高却没人来提，班次一减再减，装卸工在休息棚里等消息
scene: 码头的集装箱堆到三层高却没人来提，班次一减再减，装卸工在休息棚里等消息，连食堂也缩短了开饭时间。 Freight volumes fell for three quarters, a clear sign of economic contraction.
sceneCN: 这里 economic contraction 指「产出、就业与支出都在下降的阶段」（第 1 个义项：经济体规模整体缩小的时期）；句意为货运量连续三个季度下滑，是经济收缩的明显迹象。图中可辨识物件：堆高的集装箱、减少的班次表、休息棚、缩短营业的食堂。

pos.zh: 经济收缩；经济下行阶段

senses.title: A period of shrinking output
senses.definition: a stretch of time in which an economy produces, employs and spends less than before
senses.definitionCN: 一个经济体比此前生产更少、雇用更少、支出更少的时期
senses.example: Freight volumes fell for three quarters, a clear sign of economic contraction.
senses.exampleCN: 货运量连续三个季度下滑，是经济收缩的明显迹象。
senses.why: Contraction is the noun of a Latin verb meaning 'to draw together', so the phrase pictures the economy pulled in on itself.
senses.whyCN: contraction 是一个意为「拉到一起」的拉丁动词的名词，因此这个短语把经济想象成向内收拢。

senses.title: The downswing of the cycle
senses.definition: the falling phase of the business cycle, between one peak and the next trough
senses.definitionCN: 商业周期中下降的那一段，位于一个峰顶与下一个谷底之间
senses.example: The last economic contraction was short but steep.
senses.exampleCN: 上一轮经济收缩虽短，却很陡。
senses.why: Drawn as a wave, the falling half needs a name, and contraction is the natural opposite of expansion.
senses.whyCN: 把周期画成波浪，下降的一半就需要名字，而 contraction 正是 expansion 的自然对立面。

senses.title: A firm cutting its scale
senses.definition: the shrinking of a company through closed plants, fewer staff or narrower markets
senses.definitionCN: 企业通过关厂、减员或收缩市场而缩小
senses.example: The chain's economic contraction closed forty stores.
senses.exampleCN: 这家连锁店的规模收缩关掉了四十家门店。
senses.why: The verb applies to anything being drawn smaller, so one business can contract exactly as an economy does.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词可用于任何被拉小的事物，因此单个企业的收缩与整个经济的收缩用的是同一个词。

senses.title: Muscle contraction
senses.definition: the shortening and thickening of a muscle when it does work
senses.definitionCN: 肌肉发力时变短变粗的过程
senses.example: Each contraction of the heart pushes blood onward.
senses.exampleCN: 心脏每一次收缩都把血向前推送。
senses.why: Physiology took the literal drawing-together of fibres, which is the clearest physical instance of the root.
senses.whyCN: 生理学取用了纤维字面上的「拉到一起」，这是这个词根最清楚的物理实例。

senses.title: Shrinking in volume
senses.definition: the decrease in size of a material or object when it cools, dries or is compressed
senses.definitionCN: 材料或物体在冷却、干燥或被压缩时尺寸变小
senses.example: The contraction of the clay opened cracks along the rim.
senses.exampleCN: 陶土收缩，沿口沿裂开。
senses.why: When a body draws in, its volume falls, and the noun names that measurable change.
senses.whyCN: 物体向内收，体积就减小，这个名词指称那种可度量的变化。

senses.title: Contraction of credit
senses.definition: a fall in lending as banks tighten terms or lose confidence
senses.definitionCN: 银行收紧条件或失去信心而导致贷款减少
senses.example: Credit contraction hit small builders first.
senses.exampleCN: 信贷收缩首先打击了小型建筑商。
senses.why: Lending is one channel through which an economy draws in, and the phrase names the channel rather than the total.
senses.whyCN: 放贷是经济向内收的一条渠道，这个短语指渠道而非总量。

senses.title: Contraction of spending
senses.definition: a cut in household, business or government spending
senses.definitionCN: 家庭、企业或政府支出的削减
senses.example: Household spending contraction deepened the factory slowdown.
senses.exampleCN: 家庭支出收缩加深了工厂的放缓。
senses.why: Spending is the demand side of the same shrinking, and the phrase can point there instead of at output.
senses.whyCN: 支出是同一个缩小的需求一侧，这个短语可以指向那里而非产出。

senses.title: Contraction of the money supply
senses.definition: a decrease in the quantity of money circulating in an economy
senses.definitionCN: 经济体中流通的货币数量减少
senses.example: Monetary contraction followed the panic of that autumn.
senses.exampleCN: 货币层面的收缩紧随那年秋天的恐慌而来。
senses.why: The central bank can draw the money stock in directly, and the phrase borrows the same image for that measure.
senses.whyCN: 央行可以直接把货币存量收紧，这个短语便为那项度量借用同一个意象。

intro.en: Economic contraction joins economic, from Greek oikonomia through Latin oeconomia, with contraction, from Latin contractio, built on contrahere 'to draw together', from con- 'together' and trahere 'to draw'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: economic contraction 由 economic（出自希腊 oikonomia，经拉丁 oeconomia）与 contraction 组合而成；contraction 来自拉丁 contractio，由 contrahere「拉到一起」构成，即 con-「共同」加 trahere「拉」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Trahere meant 'to draw, to pull' and stands behind tractor, attract, extract and a large English family.
items.cn: trahere 意为「拉、拖」，是 tractor、attract、extract 以及一大族英语词的来源。

items.en: Con- 'together' plus trahere gave contrahere 'to draw together, to tighten'; it also came to mean to conclude an agreement.
items.cn: con-「共同」加 trahere 构成 contrahere「拉到一起、收紧」；它后来也指缔结协议。

items.en: The noun contractio named the drawing together of anything, from limbs to legal terms.
items.cn: 名词 contractio 指把任何东西拉到一起，从肢体到法律条款都包括。

items.en: English contraction is recorded from the sixteenth century for the shortening of words and for the action of muscles.
items.cn: 英语 contraction 自 16 世纪有记录，指词的缩短以及肌肉的动作。

items.en: The same Latin verb produced contract as a noun for an agreement, since terms are drawn together into one binding arrangement; that sense diverged from the physical one.
items.cn: 同一个拉丁动词还产生名词 contract「合同」，因为条款被拉到一起成为一份有约束力的安排；那一义与物理义分道而行。

items.en: The economic sense developed with business-cycle language in the twentieth century, when contraction became the measurable opposite of expansion.
items.cn: 经济义随 20 世纪的商业周期话语发展出来，此时 contraction 成为 expansion 可度量的对立面。

note.en: The first group holds terms often swapped for this phrase, including two from the same root that mean something else; the second holds words for things getting smaller.
note.cn: 第一组是常与本短语互换的说法，其中含两个同根却另有所指的词；第二组是「变小」的词。

entries.definition: A contraction long enough to be officially counted; contraction can be shorter and is the measurable movement itself.
entries.definitionCN: 持续到被正式计量的收缩；contraction 可以更短，且就是那个可度量的运动本身。

entries.definition: Shrinking of any kind, including muscles and word forms; the phrase narrows it to the economy.
entries.definitionCN: 任何意义上的缩小，包括肌肉与词形；短语把它收窄到经济。

entries.definition: From the same verb 'to draw together', but as a noun it means a binding agreement, not a shrinking.
entries.definitionCN: 同出「拉到一起」这个动词，但作名词时指有约束力的协议，而非缩小。

entries.definition: From constringere, built on stringere 'to bind tight': a narrowing by pressure, not a settling inward.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 constringere，词根是 stringere「束紧」：指受压变窄，而非向内收拢。

entries.definition: Any decline in activity; vaguer and milder than a measured contraction.
entries.definitionCN: 活动下滑的通称；比可度量的 contraction 更模糊、更轻。

entries.definition: A literal getting smaller, often of material or stock; it lacks the cyclical meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 字面上的变小，多指材料或存货；不带周期含义。

entries.definition: A general falling off in amount or quality; it makes no claim about measurement.
entries.definitionCN: 数量或质量的普遍下降；不涉及度量。

entries.definition: A deliberate policy of cutting spending; it may cause contraction but is a choice, not the movement.
entries.definitionCN: 有意的削减开支政策；它可能造成收缩，但那是选择而非运动本身。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: a real Latin prefix and root, a real family and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁前缀与词根、真实的同族词与真实的固定说法，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: con- 'together' plus trahere 'draw': the economy draws in on itself.
normal.cn: con-「共同」加 trahere「拉」：经济把自己往里收。

normal.en: The family runs contract, contraction, contractionary, contractile, contractor.
normal.cn: 同族词串成一线：contract、contraction、contractionary、contractile、contractor。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: sharp economic contraction, contractionary policy, global contraction.
normal.cn: 固定说法：急剧经济收缩、紧缩性政策、全球收缩。

normal.en: In cycle talk contraction is the mirror of expansion.
normal.cn: 在周期话语中，contraction 是 expansion 的镜像。

normal.en: Keep it apart from constriction, whose root is stringere 'to bind'.
normal.cn: 把它与 constriction 分开，后者词根是 stringere「束紧」。

abstract.en: Picture stacked containers that nobody comes to collect.
abstract.cn: 想象堆高的集装箱，没人来提。

abstract.en: Picture a shift board with more and more lines crossed out.
abstract.cn: 想象班次表上被划掉的线越来越多。

abstract.en: Picture a hand slowly closing around a coin.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手慢慢把一枚硬币握紧。

examples.en: A sharp economic contraction usually hits young workers first.
examples.cn: 急剧的经济收缩通常最先冲击年轻工人。

examples.en: The central bank cut rates to pull the economy out of contraction.
examples.cn: 央行降息，力图把经济拉出收缩。

examples.en: Credit contraction turned a small shock into a long slump.
examples.cn: 信贷收缩把一次小冲击拖成了长期低迷。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「economic（经济的）+ contraction（往里收）」——整块经济往内收 → 经济收缩

root: economic 出自希腊 oikonomia「家务管理」（oikos 家 + nomos 管理），经拉丁 oeconomia 与法语；contraction 出自拉丁 contrahere「拉到一起」= con-「共同」+ trahere「拉」→ contractio；同根名词 contract 指合同，义已分化。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one drawing-in: the economy pulls inward, and that pulling is read as a cycle phase, as a firm's shrink, as a muscle shortening, as a volume loss, as less credit, as less spending and finally as less money.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个「向内收」展开：经济往里收，这个收拢再依次被读作周期阶段、企业缩小、肌肉变短、体积减小、更少信贷、更少支出，最后是更少货币。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: stacked containers nobody collects, a shift board crossed out, and a hand closing around a coin.
core.cn: 核心意象：无人来提的堆高集装箱、被划掉的班次表，以及慢慢握紧硬币的手。

branches.en: OUTPUT AND CYCLE: the whole economy pulls in, and that pull is the falling half of a wave.
branches.cn: 产出与周期：整个经济向内收，这个收拢就是波浪下降的一半。

branches.en: FIRM AND SPENDING: one business shrinks, and households cut what they buy.
branches.cn: 企业与支出：单个企业缩小，家庭削减购买。

branches.en: BODY AND MATTER: a muscle shortens, and a material loses volume.
branches.cn: 身体与物质：肌肉变短，材料失去体积。

branches.en: CREDIT: lending is the channel through which the pull runs fastest.
branches.cn: 信贷：放贷是这种收拢传导最快的渠道。

branches.en: MONEY: the central bank draws the stock of money in by design.
branches.cn: 货币：央行有意把货币存量收紧。

intro.en: The phrase combines a Greek-derived adjective and a Latin noun; the noun can be read as a prefix, a verb root and a process suffix.
intro.cn: 这个短语由一个希腊来源的形容词与一个拉丁名词组合而成；名词部分可拆成前缀、动词词根与过程后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin trahere 'to draw' gives contract, contraction, tractor, attract and extract; con- adds the idea of drawing together.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 trahere「拉」衍生出 contract、contraction、tractor、attract 与 extract；con- 增添「拉到一起」的意思。

items.example: The prefix makes the drawing collective.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀使「拉」成为向内的合拢。

items.example: The root runs through tractor and attract.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根贯穿 tractor 与 attract。

items.example: The compound also named the making of an agreement.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合形式还指缔结协议。

items.example: The Latin noun gave English contraction.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词给出英语 contraction。

items.example: The suffix turns the verb into a process noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词变成过程名词。

items.structure: contract (English verb and noun from Latin contractus)
items.example: The two senses split long ago.
The adjective marks policy that deliberately tightens.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词标记有意收紧的政策。

items.example: Muscle fibre is contractile tissue.
items.exampleCN: 肌纤维是可收缩的组织。

definition_zh: 营养学家；营养师
definition_en: a person trained in the science of nutrition who advises people on what to eat for health
core_image: 一个人站在餐盘旁，把食物按营养素分类、称量，并写下饮食建议
scene: 这里指「营养学家」。 The nutritionist put the patient on a diet rich in iron and fibre.
sceneCN: 这里 nutritionist 指「临床营养师」（第 2 个义项：在医院里为病人设计治疗饮食的专业人员）；句意：营养师给这位病人安排了富含铁和膳食纤维的饮食。图中可辨识物件：餐盘、食物模型、营养成分表、病历夹。

pos.zh: 营养学家；营养师（受过营养学训练、为个人或群体提供饮食建议的人）

senses.title: Nutrition scientist
senses.titleCN: 营养学家：研究营养素如何作用于人体
senses.definition: a scientist who studies how nutrients affect growth, health and disease
senses.definitionCN: 研究营养素如何影响生长、健康与疾病的科学家
senses.example: The nutritionist measured the children's iron intake over a month.
senses.exampleCN: 这位营养学家测量了孩子们一个月的铁摄入量。
senses.why: Latin nutrire 'to nourish' plus -ist 'one who practises' first named a specialist in the young science of nutrition; the laboratory sense is the oldest one.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 nutrire「滋养」加 -ist「从事者」，最初指新兴营养科学中的专业人员；实验室研究义是最早的义项。

senses.title: Clinical dietitian
senses.titleCN: 临床营养师：为病人设计治疗饮食
senses.definition: a specialist, usually in a hospital, who plans meals and tube feeding for patients with medical conditions
senses.definitionCN: 通常在医院工作，为患病者安排饮食与管饲方案的专业人员
senses.example: The nutritionist put the patient on a diet rich in iron and fibre.
senses.exampleCN: 营养师给这位病人安排了富含铁和膳食纤维的饮食。
senses.why: Hospitals needed a staff member to turn a diagnosis into a menu, so the word moved from the laboratory to the ward.
senses.whyCN: 医院需要有人把诊断变成菜单，于是这个词从实验室走进了病房。

senses.title: Sports nutritionist
senses.titleCN: 运动营养师：为训练与比赛配餐
senses.definition: a practitioner who adjusts energy, protein and fluid intake for athletes and training cycles
senses.definitionCN: 为运动员和训练周期调整能量、蛋白质与液体摄入的从业者
senses.example: The team hired a nutritionist to plan meals before the marathon.
senses.exampleCN: 球队聘请了一位营养师来规划马拉松前的饮食。
senses.why: Sport created a market for timed eating: nutrients are treated as fuel for a scheduled performance.
senses.whyCN: 竞技体育催生了「按时吃饭」的市场：营养素被当作按赛程供应的燃料。

senses.title: Public health nutritionist
senses.titleCN: 公共营养师：面向人群而非个人
senses.definition: a professional who designs programmes and policies about diet for whole communities
senses.definitionCN: 为整个社区设计饮食方案与政策的专业人员
senses.example: Public health nutritionists pushed for free school breakfasts.
senses.exampleCN: 公共营养师推动学校提供免费早餐。
senses.why: The same expertise is applied to populations, so the unit of work changes from one plate to a thousand plates.
senses.whyCN: 同样的专业知识被用到人群层面，工作单位从一张餐盘变成上千张餐盘。

senses.title: Food industry adviser
senses.titleCN: 食品行业营养顾问：参与配方与标签
senses.definition: a nutrition expert employed by a food company to shape recipes, claims and labels
senses.definitionCN: 受雇于食品企业，参与配方、营养声称与标签制定的营养专家
senses.example: The company's nutritionist rewrote the label to meet the new sugar rules.
senses.exampleCN: 公司的营养顾问重写了标签，以满足新的糖含量规定。
senses.why: Regulation turned nutritional knowledge into a commercial and legal service, a sense the word acquired in the twentieth century.
senses.whyCN: 法规把营养知识变成商业与法律服务，这是该词在 20 世纪获得的义项。

senses.title: Researcher and writer
senses.titleCN: 营养研究者与科普作者
senses.definition: a person who studies diets and publishes findings or advice for the general reader
senses.definitionCN: 研究饮食并面向普通读者发表研究结果或建议的人
senses.example: The nutritionist wrote a column debunking detox diets.
senses.exampleCN: 这位营养学者写专栏驳斥「排毒饮食」。
senses.why: Popular publishing gave the title a public voice, distinct from both the clinic and the company.
senses.whyCN: 大众出版让这个头衔有了公共发声的角色，与诊所和企业的身份都不同。

senses.title: Private consultant
senses.titleCN: 私人营养顾问：一对一收费咨询
senses.definition: a practitioner who sells one-to-one dietary advice outside hospitals and sports clubs
senses.definitionCN: 在医院与运动队之外，以一对一方式出售饮食建议的从业者
senses.example: She sees a nutritionist privately every other week.
senses.exampleCN: 她每两周自费看一次私人营养顾问。
senses.why: The word follows the modern shift of advice into a paid service sold directly to the client.
senses.whyCN: 这个词跟随现代趋势，把建议变成直接卖给客户的付费服务。

senses.title: Animal nutritionist
senses.titleCN: 动物营养师：配饲料与养殖方案
senses.definition: an expert who formulates feed for farm animals, pets or zoo animals
senses.definitionCN: 为家畜、宠物或动物园动物配制饲料的专家
senses.example: The farm's nutritionist balanced the ration for the dairy herd.
senses.exampleCN: 农场的动物营养师为奶牛群平衡了日粮。
senses.why: Animal husbandry adopted the same science early, because feed conversion is measured in money.
senses.whyCN: 畜牧业很早就采用了同一门科学，因为饲料转化率直接以金钱计量。

senses.title: Self-styled expert
senses.titleCN: 「营养大师」：无资质却自称专家（含贬义）
senses.definition: loosely, a person who gives diet advice without formal qualification, often used with disapproval
senses.definitionCN: 泛指未经正式资质却提供饮食建议的人，常带不赞许意味
senses.example: Online nutritionists sell supplements with no evidence behind them.
senses.exampleCN: 网上的「营养大师」推销毫无证据支持的补充剂。
senses.why: Because the title is unregulated in many places, it can be claimed by anyone, and the word gained this sceptical edge.
senses.whyCN: 由于许多地方并不监管这个头衔，任何人都能自称，这个词因此带上了怀疑色彩。

intro.en: Nutritionist is Latin nutrire 'to nourish' plus the agent suffix -ist, mediated by the noun nutrition. The dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: nutritionist 由拉丁 nutrire「滋养」加表人后缀 -ist 构成，中间经由名词 nutrition。以下年代均为约数。

items.en: Latin nutrire meant 'to nourish, to suckle'. The related noun nutrix 'wet nurse' shows the earliest picture: feeding is something one person does for another.
items.cn: 拉丁 nutrire 意为「滋养、哺乳」。相关名词 nutrix「乳母」显示了最早的画面：喂养是一个人替另一个人做的事。

items.en: Nutritio, nutritionis named the act of nourishing. Classical writers used it for feeding and rearing rather than for a modern science.
items.cn: nutritio、nutritionis 指滋养这一动作。古典作家用它表示喂养与抚育，而不是现代意义上的科学。

items.en: English nutrition entered in the fourteenth century through Old French, still meaning the act of nourishing or being nourished.
items.cn: 英语 nutrition 于 14 世纪经由古法语进入，仍指滋养或被滋养的动作。

items.en: In the nineteenth century chemists began measuring calories, proteins and minerals, and nutrition became a laboratory discipline with its own methods.
items.cn: 19 世纪化学家开始测量热量、蛋白质与矿物质，营养学成为一门有自身方法的实验学科。

items.en: The agent noun nutritionist is recorded in the early twentieth century, around the 1920s. The exact first citation is uncertain, and the title has never been legally protected in many countries.
items.cn: 表人名词 nutritionist 记录于 20 世纪初，约在 1920 年代。最早的确切书证年代存疑，而且这个头衔在许多国家从未受法律保护。

items.en: Source uncertainty: the first English date of nutritionist is not firmly fixed, and the deeper Indo-European root behind Latin nutrire is a reconstruction, not a recorded form.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代与更深词根）：nutritionist 的英语首见年代无定论；拉丁 nutrire 背后的更深印欧词根属重构形式，并非有记录的实际词。

note.en: The first group holds words from the same Latin family or the same professional field that are easily confused; the second holds near-synonyms for the person who gives dietary advice.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁词族或同一职业领域、容易混淆的词；第二组是「提供饮食建议的人」的近义词。

entries.definition: In many countries a legally protected title requiring registration and clinical training; nutritionist is often the unregulated word.
entries.definitionCN: 在许多国家是受法律保护、需要注册与临床训练的头衔；nutritionist 则常是不受监管的说法。

entries.definition: The science or the process of nourishing. It names the subject, while nutritionist names the practitioner.
entries.definitionCN: 指营养学或滋养过程，命名的是学科，而 nutritionist 命名的是从业者。

entries.definition: Means 'full of nutrients', and is said of food rather than of people or careers.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「有营养的」，用于形容食物，而不是人或职业。

entries.definition: Means 'concerning nutrition', as in nutritional value; it describes a property, not a person.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「营养方面的」，如 nutritional value；它描述属性，不指人。

entries.definition: A near-synonym in hospitals, but the two titles differ in law and training in many countries.
entries.definitionCN: 在医院语境里是近义词，但在许多国家两者在法律地位与训练要求上并不相同。

entries.definition: A person who mainly helps a client keep to a plan; coaching stresses habits, not clinical assessment.
entries.definitionCN: 主要帮客户坚持计划的人；coaching 强调习惯，而不是临床评估。

entries.definition: An expert in how food is processed, preserved and formulated; the focus is the product rather than the eater.
entries.definitionCN: 研究食品加工、保藏与配方的专家，关注产品而非进食者。

entries.definition: A practitioner of a alternative tradition that may include diet advice; the training and evidence base differ from nutrition science.
entries.definitionCN: 属于另一套替代医学传统的从业者，可能也提供饮食建议，但其训练与证据基础不同于营养科学。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: nutri- 'nourish' + -tion 'the field' + -ist 'the person'.
normal.cn: nutri-「滋养」+ -tion「领域」+ -ist「人」。

normal.en: The family runs nutrition, nutritional, nutritious, nutrient and nourish.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 nutrition、nutritional、nutritious、nutrient、nourish。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the workplace: clinical nutritionist, sports nutritionist, registered nutritionist.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出工作场景：临床营养师、运动营养师、注册营养师。

normal.en: -ist names a person, -tion names a field, -ous describes food.
normal.cn: -ist 指人，-tion 指领域，-ous 形容食物。

normal.en: dietitian is the regulated title; nutritionist is the looser one.
normal.cn: dietitian 是受监管的头衔，nutritionist 则较宽松。

abstract.en: Picture a plate divided like a pie chart, each slice a nutrient group.
abstract.cn: 想象一只餐盘被分成饼图，每一块代表一类营养素。

abstract.en: Picture a small label being turned over to read the numbers on the back.
abstract.cn: 想象有人翻过一张小标签，读背面的数字。

abstract.en: Picture a prescription pad on which meals are written instead of pills.
abstract.cn: 想象一张处方笺，上面写的是饭菜而不是药片。

examples.en: A nutritionist helped the team plan meals before the marathon.
examples.cn: 一位营养师帮球队规划了马拉松前的饮食。

examples.en: The hospital's nutritionist adjusted her diet after surgery.
examples.cn: 医院的营养师在她手术后调整了饮食。

examples.en: Nutritionists disagree about how much protein older adults need.
examples.cn: 营养学家对老年人需要多少蛋白质存在分歧。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「nutri 滋养 + tion 学问 + ist 人」——研究怎么滋养身体的人 → nutritionist 营养师

root: 拉丁 nutrire「滋养」→ nutritio「营养」→ 英语 nutrition + -ist「从事者」→ nutritionist。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one movement: knowledge about nourishing a body leaves the laboratory and is applied to a patient, an athlete, a population, a product, a farm animal, or merely sold as advice.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿同一个动作展开：关于「如何滋养身体」的知识离开实验室，被用到一个病人、一名运动员、一群居民、一件产品、一头农场动物身上，或仅仅被当作建议出售。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a plate being measured and a set of food rules being written down.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只餐盘被称量，一套饮食规则被写下来。

branches.en: LABORATORY AND WARD: the same expertise serves both the research bench and the hospital bedside.
branches.cn: 实验室与病房：同一套专业知识既服务研究台，也服务医院床边。

branches.en: PERFORMANCE AND PUBLIC HEALTH: nutrients are planned for a race or for a whole generation of schoolchildren.
branches.cn: 竞技与公共健康：营养素既为一场比赛安排，也为整整一代学童安排。

branches.en: THE MARKET: food companies hire the same knowledge to shape recipes, claims and labels.
branches.cn: 市场一端：食品企业购买同一套知识来塑造配方、声称与标签。

branches.en: VOICE AND FEE: the title also names a public writer and a private consultant paid by the hour.
branches.cn: 发声与收费：这个头衔也指公共写作者和按小时收费的私人顾问。

branches.en: BEYOND THE CLINIC: the word reaches farm animals, and it can also be claimed by people with no qualification at all.
branches.cn: 诊所之外：这个词延伸到农场动物，也可能被完全无资质的人拿来自称。

intro.en: Nutritionist is a Latin root of nourishing, a noun of action, and an agent suffix: nutri- plus -tion plus -ist.
intro.cn: nutritionist 由表示「滋养」的拉丁词根、动作名词后缀与表人后缀构成：nutri- 加 -tion 再加 -ist。

latinIntro.en: Latin nutrire 'to nourish' supplies nutrition, nutritious, nutrient, nutriment and, through Old French, the verb nourish; nutrix 'wet nurse' belongs to the same family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 nutrire「滋养」衍生了 nutrition、nutritious、nutrient、nutriment，并经古法语产生动词 nourish；nutrix「乳母」也属同一词族。

senses.exampleCN: 我们在车站附近的小馆吃饭，只能站着。

definition_zh: 市场竞争；市场中多个卖者或买者为争夺同一批顾客、合同与资源而相互角逐的状态；竞争政策所规范的对象
definition_en: the state in which several sellers or buyers contend for the same customers, contracts or resources, each trying to win business away from the others
core_image: 一条街上几家卖同样货品的铺子并排开着，顾客一走近便被各家招手，铺主不断改价、换招牌、添赠品，只求把人引进自己门里
scene: 同一街区里开着几家卖同样货品的铺子，顾客一走近就被各家招手，铺主不断改价、换招牌、添赠品，只为把客人引进自己门里；傍晚一算账，谁家让价让得多，谁家门口就排得长。 Market competition keeps every one of them watching the others' prices.
sceneCN: 几家同类铺子在同一条街上争夺同一批过路人，彼此盯着对方的标价不断调整。句中的 market competition 指「多个主体争夺同一批顾客的状态」（第 1 个义项：同业者为同一批买主相互角逐）。图中可辨识物件：并排的店面、手写价牌、赠品篮、排队的人。

pos.zh: 市场竞争（指争夺状态，通常不可数；指不同细分市场中的多场竞争时可用复数）
