senses.title: Several sellers chasing the same buyers
senses.titleCN: 多个卖者追逐同一批买主
senses.definition: the ordinary situation in which two or more firms offer similar goods to the same group of customers
senses.definitionCN: 两家或更多厂商向同一群顾客提供相似货物的一般情形
senses.example: Market competition forces the two chains to match each other's opening hours.
senses.exampleCN: 市场竞争迫使两家连锁店把营业时间对齐。
senses.why: competition goes back to a Latin verb for seeking the same thing together, and market names the arena, so the phrase says that several parties seek one prize in one place.
senses.whyCN: competition 上溯一个表示「共同追求同一物」的拉丁动词，market 指场所，因此这个短语是说：多方在同一场所追逐同一个目标。

senses.title: Rivalry conducted through price
senses.titleCN: 以价格手段进行的争夺
senses.definition: contention carried on by cutting prices, offering discounts or matching a rival's rate
senses.definitionCN: 通过降价、折扣或与对手同价来进行的争夺
senses.example: Market competition in the budget sector has pushed fares down for a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 廉价市场的竞争已把票价压低了十年。
senses.why: price is the fastest lever a seller can pull, so the general rivalry is often narrowed to the one instrument that shows up first on a price board.
senses.whyCN: 价格是卖者能拉动的最快的杠杆，因此笼统的角逐常被收窄为最先写在价牌上的那件工具。

senses.title: Rivalry through quality and brands
senses.titleCN: 以品质、品牌与服务进行的争夺
senses.definition: contention carried on by improving quality, design, service or advertising rather than by cutting the price
senses.definitionCN: 通过提升品质、设计、服务或广告而非降价来进行的争夺
senses.example: Where fares are fixed by law, market competition shifts to legroom and punctuality.
senses.exampleCN: 当票价由法律规定时，市场竞争便转向腿部空间与准点率。
senses.why: once price is off the table, sellers must differentiate, so the word's field extends from the price tag to everything else a buyer weighs.
senses.whyCN: 一旦价格不可动，卖者只能在别处做出区别，于是这个词的范围从价签扩展到买方所权衡的一切。

senses.title: The benchmark of many small rivals
senses.titleCN: 作为基准的充分竞争状态
senses.definition: the idealised condition in which so many sellers exist that none can influence price, used as a measuring rod
senses.definitionCN: 一种理想化状态：卖者多到无人能影响价格，常被用作衡量的标尺
senses.example: The textbook treats market competition as a benchmark against which real industries are judged.
senses.exampleCN: 教科书把市场竞争当作评判现实产业的基准。
senses.why: theory needs a limiting case, so the phrase also names the pole of perfect rivalry rather than any observable market.
senses.whyCN: 理论需要一个极值情形，因此这个短语也指「充分角逐」的那一端，而非任何可观察的市场。

senses.title: The object of competition law
senses.titleCN: 竞争法所保护与规范的对象
senses.definition: the rivalry that authorities protect by blocking mergers, cartels and abuses of dominance
senses.definitionCN: 主管机关通过阻止合并、卡特尔与滥用支配地位来保护的角逐
senses.example: The case turned on whether a rebate scheme had removed market competition in the dairy aisle.
senses.exampleCN: 该案的争点在于返利方案是否消除了乳品货架上的市场竞争。
senses.why: law personifies the phrase as something that can be harmed or preserved, which is why it appears as the object of enforcement verbs.
senses.whyCN: 法律把这个短语当作可被损害、也可被保全的对象，因此它常作执法动词的宾语。

senses.title: Rivalry between regions or states
senses.titleCN: 地区或辖区之间为吸引投资而竞争
senses.definition: contention among jurisdictions that cut taxes or offer subsidies to attract the same firms
senses.definitionCN: 各辖区为吸引同一批企业而减税或提供补贴的争夺
senses.example: Market competition between cities produced a costly race of tax breaks.
senses.exampleCN: 城市之间的市场竞争演变成一场代价高昂的减税竞赛。
senses.why: the sellers in this reading are governments offering a location, so the same frame is transferred from shops to jurisdictions.
senses.whyCN: 这种读法中的「卖者」是提供落户地的政府，于是同一框架从店铺转移到了辖区。

senses.title: A selection mechanism that weeds out firms
senses.titleCN: 淘汰落后者的一种选择机制
senses.definition: the process by which inefficient sellers lose customers and exit while efficient ones expand
senses.definitionCN: 低效卖者失去顾客并退出、高效卖者扩张的过程
senses.example: Market competition drove three of the seven mills out of business within four years.
senses.exampleCN: 市场竞争使七家磨坊中的三家在四年内停业。
senses.why: rivalry does not merely set prices, it also decides who survives, so the phrase can name a sorting process rather than a state.
senses.whyCN: 角逐不仅定出价格，也决定谁存活，因此这个短语可指名一个筛选过程，而非一种状态。

senses.title: Contention inside a segment or platform
senses.titleCN: 细分市场或平台内部的争夺
senses.definition: rivalry confined to one product segment, or played out between platforms that host other sellers
senses.definitionCN: 局限于某一产品细分的争夺，或在承载其他卖者的平台之间展开的争夺
senses.example: Market competition among delivery apps now turns on who controls the rider network.
senses.exampleCN: 配送应用之间的市场竞争，如今取决于谁掌握骑手网络。
senses.why: the phrase scales down to a niche and up to a platform layer, because the contending parties can be any sellers sharing one pool of demand.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语既可缩小到一个细分位，也可放大到一个平台层，因为相互角逐的可以是共享同一需求池的任何卖者。

intro.en: Market competition pairs a Latin trade noun with a Latin noun of striving. Market goes back to mercatus 'a place of trading'; competition goes back to competere, literally 'to seek together', built from com- 'together' and petere 'to seek, to head for'.
intro.cn: market competition 把一个拉丁的交易名词与一个拉丁的「力争」名词配在一起。market 上溯 mercatus「交易场所」；competition 上溯 competere，字面是「共同追求」，由表示「共同」的前缀与 petere「寻求、奔向」构成。

items.en: Petere meant 'to seek, to make for, to attack'. It is generally thought to come from a root for rushing at something, but the older form is a reconstruction, not a recorded word.
items.cn: petere 意为「寻求、奔向、攻击」。一般认为它出自表示「扑向某物」的词根，但更早的形式是重构形式，而非有记录的词。

items.en: Com- 'together' plus petere produced competere, whose first sense was 'to meet, to come together, to coincide'. Only in later Latin did it take on 'to strive after the same thing, to contend'.
items.cn: 表示「共同」的前缀加 petere 构成 competere，其本义是「相遇、会合、恰好一致」。到较晚的拉丁语中，它才带上「争夺同一物、相争」的意思。

items.en: The noun competitio named the act of seeking something together, and in legal and later usage it named a claim laid by several parties to one thing, hence a dispute.
items.cn: 名词 competitio 指「共同追求某物」的行为，在法律及后世用法中指多方对同一物提出主张，因而带上争执之意。

items.en: Competition reached English through Old French in the sixteenth century, bringing the sense of rivalry between persons or traders rather than the older sense of coincidence.
items.cn: competition 于十六世纪经古法语进入英语，带来的是人与人、商人与商人之间的角逐义，而非较早的「恰好一致」义。

items.en: The full phrase became standard with industrial organization and competition policy in the twentieth century, when rivalry among sellers was named, measured and regulated as a distinct object.
items.cn: 完整短语在二十世纪的产业组织理论与竞争政策中成为标准说法，卖者之间的角逐从此被命名、测量并作为独立对象加以规范。

items.en: Source uncertain: no single citation fixes the moment when the Latin verb shifted from 'meet' to 'contend', and the pre-Latin root of petere is unsettled, so the boundary dates given here are approximations.
items.cn: 来源不确定：没有单一书证能确定这个拉丁动词由「相遇」转为「相争」的时刻，petere 在拉丁语之前的词根亦无定论，此处给出的分界年代只是约数。

note.en: Group one shares the Latin striving root but names a capacity, a person or a quality instead of the contest itself; group two names neighbouring ideas in the same contest, each with a narrower reach.
note.cn: 第一组共用拉丁「力争」词根，但指能力、人物或性质，而非角逐本身；第二组指同一场角逐中的邻近概念，各自范围更窄。

entries.definition: The ability of a firm or country to hold its own against rivals; it is the strength brought to the contest, not the contest itself.
entries.definitionCN: 企业或国家与对手抗衡的能力；它是带入角逐的实力，而非角逐本身。

entries.definition: One of the parties doing the contending; it names a participant, whereas the target names the relation between participants.
entries.definitionCN: 参与角逐的其中一方；它指参与者，而目标短语指参与者之间的关系。

entries.definition: The adjective describing a market or a price that can win business; the target is the noun for the process the adjective describes.
entries.definitionCN: 描述市场或价格足以赢得生意的形容词；目标短语则是该形容词所指过程的名称。

entries.definition: A continuing state of striving between two parties; it stresses duration and personal antagonism, which a market phrase does not.
entries.definitionCN: 两方持续力争的状态；强调持续性与人对人的敌意，市场短语不含这两层。

entries.definition: A contest fought only by repeated price cuts; it is a single episode inside the target, not the whole relation.
entries.definitionCN: 只靠反复降价进行的争夺；它是目标状态中的一段插曲，而非整段关系。

entries.definition: The ease with which a newcomer could enter and displace an incumbent; it measures a threat behind the contest rather than the contest.
entries.definitionCN: 新来者进入并取代在位者的容易程度；它衡量角逐背后的威胁，而非角逐本身。

entries.definition: The body of law that protects rivalry; it is the policy instrument aimed at the target, not the target.
entries.definitionCN: 保护角逐的法律体系；它是指向目标状态的政策工具，而非目标状态。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin verb 'to seek together', real relatives and real phrases from competition policy.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁动词「共同追求」、真实同族词，以及竞争政策中的真实说法。

normal.en: Competition rests on competere, com- 'together' plus petere 'to seek': two parties seeking one thing is already the whole picture.
normal.cn: competition 基于 competere，即表示「共同」的前缀加 petere「寻求」：两方共追一物，画面已然完整。

normal.en: The old sense was 'to meet or coincide', which is why the same root also gives competent, a word about fitting the case.
normal.cn: 旧义是「相遇、相合」，同一词根因此也给出 competent，一个表示「合于其事」的词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the intensity: intense market competition, fair market competition, shielded from market competition.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出强度：激烈的市场竞争、公平的市场竞争、受保护而免受市场竞争。

normal.en: Policy vocabulary travels with the phrase: competition policy, antitrust enforcement, a merger review.
normal.cn: 政策词汇与这个短语同行：竞争政策、反垄断执法、合并审查。

normal.en: The phrase is also a benchmark, so textbooks set it beside monopoly and oligopoly on the same scale.
normal.cn: 这个短语同时是一个基准，因此教科书把它与垄断、寡头放在同一标尺上。

abstract.en: Picture several shopkeepers on one street all watching the same passer-by and stepping forward at the same moment.
abstract.cn: 想象一条街上几个店主盯着同一位过路人，并在同一刻一起迎上前去。

abstract.en: Picture a price board rewritten every morning by each shop, then compared with the board across the road.
abstract.cn: 想象每家铺子每天早上重写价牌，然后与对街那家的价牌相比。

abstract.en: Picture a race in which the finish line is the customer's hand reaching for one counter out of several.
abstract.cn: 想象一场赛跑，终点线是顾客的手在几个柜台之间伸向其中一个。

examples.en: Intense market competition has cut the average price of a solar panel by more than half in a decade.
examples.cn: 激烈的市场竞争使太阳能板均价在十年间下降了一半以上。

examples.en: The regulator blocked the merger on the ground that it would remove market competition in two regional routes.
examples.cn: 监管机构阻止该合并，理由是它将消除两条区域航线上的市场竞争。

examples.en: Where a service is shielded from market competition, providers tend to answer to budgets rather than to users.
examples.cn: 当某项服务免受市场竞争时，提供者往往对预算负责，而非对使用者负责。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「market（市场）+ competition（比赛）」——把集市当成一场比赛：几家铺子同抢一批客人，谁价低、谁货好，谁就得分。

root: 拉丁 mercatus「市场、交易」← mercari「做买卖」← merx（属格 mercis）「货物」；拉丁 competere「共同追求」= 表示「共同」的前缀 + petere「寻求、扑向」，晚期拉丁转为「相争」，名词 competitio 经古法语 competition 入英语；短语为二十世纪产业组织与竞争政策术语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses unfold from one Latin verb meaning to seek the same thing together: first many sellers chase one crowd, then they chase it by price, then by quality, then the chase is idealized into a benchmark, protected by law, transferred to cities, read as a weeding-out process and finally confined to a segment or a platform.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一个意为「共同追求同一物」的拉丁动词展开：先是多个卖者追同一群人，继而以价格追、以品质追，随后这场追逐被理想化为基准、被法律保护、被移用到城市之间、被读成淘汰过程，最后被限定在某个细分或某个平台之内。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: several shops on one street stepping forward at the same moment toward the same customer.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条街上几家铺子在同一刻朝同一位顾客迎上前去。

branches.en: THE BASE AND THE FIRST LEVER: many sellers share one pool of buyers, and the quickest way to pull them over is the price board.
branches.cn: 基本局面与第一根杠杆：多个卖者共享一个买主池，而把人拉过来最快的办法是价牌。

branches.en: THE SECOND LEVER AND THE LIMIT: with price fixed, rivalry moves to quality, and pushed to its limit it becomes the theorist's benchmark.
branches.cn: 第二根杠杆与极值：价格被固定时，角逐转向品质；把它推到极值，便成了理论家的基准。

branches.en: GUARDED AND RELOCATED: the law treats the contest as a thing to protect, and the same frame is then moved from shops to cities.
branches.cn: 被守护与被移用：法律把这场角逐当作需要保护之物，同一框架随后从店铺移到了城市。

branches.en: THE SORTING: beyond prices, the contest decides which sellers stay and which close their doors.
branches.cn: 筛选：除定出价格之外，角逐还决定哪些卖者留下、哪些关门。

branches.en: THE NARROW ARENA: the same chase can be scaled down to one niche or up to a platform that hosts the sellers.
branches.cn: 更窄的场地：同一场追逐可缩小到一个细分位，也可放大到承载卖者的平台。

intro.en: The phrase is a compound of two nouns, and its second half is itself a Latin verb plus a prefix and a noun suffix, so the whole can be read morpheme by morpheme.
intro.cn: 这个短语由两个名词合成，后半部分本身又是一个拉丁动词加上前缀与名词后缀，因此整体可以按语素逐个读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin com- and petere build competere, competitio and the English family compete, competitor, competitive; mercatus supplies market and merchant.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语中表示「共同」的前缀与 petere 构成 competere、competitio，以及英语词族 compete、competitor、competitive；mercatus 提供 market 与 merchant。

items.example: The prefix marks two parties acting on one object.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标记两方作用于同一对象。

items.structure: Latin verb, third conjugation, 'to seek, head for'
items.meaning: to seek, to make for, to attack
items.example: The verb supplies the striving at the heart of the word.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供这个词核心处的「力争」。

items.meaning: to seek together, then to contend
items.example: Competere first meant to meet, and later to strive against.
items.exampleCN: competere 最初意为相遇，后来意为相争。

items.structure: Latin suffix forming a noun of action
items.meaning: the act or process of doing
items.example: Competere plus the suffix yields the noun of striving.
items.exampleCN: competere 加这个后缀构成表示「力争」的名词。

items.example: Competition entered English with the sense of rivalry.
items.exampleCN: competition 带着「角逐」之义进入英语。

items.meaningCN: 有胜出倾向的；竞争性的
items.example: A competitive price is one that can take business from a rival.
items.exampleCN: 有竞争力的价格是能从对手那里抢走生意的价格。

items.example: Each competitor watches the others' moves.
items.exampleCN: 每个竞争者都盯着其他人的动作。

items.meaning: the quality of being able to contend
items.meaningCN: 能够角逐的性质；竞争力
items.example: The index ranks countries by competitiveness.
items.exampleCN: 该指数按竞争力给各国排名。

items.example: An uncompetitive price loses the contract.
items.exampleCN: 无竞争力的价格会丢掉合同。

items.meaning: a place of trade, and demand itself
items.meaningCN: 交易场所，也指需求本身
items.example: Market supplies the arena in which the contending happens.
items.exampleCN: market 提供角逐发生的场所。

latinEntries.meaning: to seek, to head for, to attack

definition_zh: 社会互动；社会交往；人与人之间的相互往来
definition_en: the reciprocal action and communication that takes place between people
core_image: 两个人隔着桌子一来一往地递东西，一个递出，一个接住，动作始终不断
scene: 在菜市场里，摊主与熟客一边挑菜一边聊天，一个问价，一个还价，话头来回接住。 Everyday social interaction in the market keeps neighbours informed and ties them together.
sceneCN: 句中 social interaction 指摊主与顾客之间你一言我一语、彼此回应的往来（第 1 个义项：人与人之间相互动作与交流的基本形态）；句意为市场里的日常社会互动让邻里互通消息、彼此联结。图中可辨识物件：菜筐、秤、零钱、写价目的纸牌。

pos.zh: 社会互动；社会交往（可数或不可数）

senses.title: Reciprocal action between people
senses.titleCN: 人与人之间相互动作与交流的基本形态
senses.definition: the general process in which people act toward one another and each response invites a further response
senses.definitionCN: 人们彼此做出行动、每次回应又引出下一次回应的总体过程
senses.example: Everyday social interaction in the market keeps neighbours informed and ties them together.
senses.exampleCN: 市场里的日常社会互动让邻里互通消息、彼此联结。
senses.why: interaction joins a prefix meaning 'between' to a verb meaning 'do, drive', so its core is action that passes back and forth rather than action in one direction.
senses.whyCN: interaction 把表示「在……之间」的前缀加到表示「做、驱动」的动词上，因此核心是来回传递的动作，而非单向动作。

senses.title: A single encounter
senses.definition: one bounded occasion of people dealing with each other, with a beginning and an end
senses.definitionCN: 人们彼此打交道的一个有始有终的具体场合
senses.example: A brief social interaction at the bus stop turned into a job offer.
senses.exampleCN: 公交站一次短暂的社会互动后来变成了一份工作机会。
senses.why: because the process sense can be counted off into episodes, the phrase also names one occasion, much as a conversation can be counted.
senses.whyCN: 因为过程义可以切分为一个个片段，这个短语也指单次场合，正如谈话可以计数一样。

senses.title: A sustained pattern of dealings
senses.definition: regular, repeated contact between the same people or communities over a long period
senses.definitionCN: 同一些人或社群在长时期内规律而反复的接触
senses.example: The two villages have kept up social interaction through market days for generations.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个村子靠赶集日维持社会交往，已经延续了好几代人。
senses.why: when single encounters repeat, they harden into a pattern, and the phrase shifts from the event to the standing relation between the parties.
senses.whyCN: 单次接触反复发生便固化为格局，短语于是从「事件」转向各方之间长期存在的关系。

senses.title: Turn-taking in face-to-face talk
senses.titleCN: 面对面交谈中的轮流发言
senses.definition: the moment-by-moment coordination of speech, gaze and gesture when people talk in person
senses.definitionCN: 人们当面交谈时对说话、目光与手势的即时协调
senses.example: Group size shapes how much talk each person contributes to a social interaction.
senses.exampleCN: 群体规模会影响每个人在一次社会互动中贡献多少话语。
senses.why: the micro-sociological sense narrows the general process to the second-by-second mechanics by which turns are offered and taken.
senses.whyCN: 微观社会学义把一般过程收窄到「话轮如何让出与接住」的逐秒机制。

senses.title: Mediated and online contact
senses.definition: interaction carried on through text, platforms or calls rather than physical presence
senses.definitionCN: 通过文字、平台或通话而非身在现场进行的互动
senses.example: Online social interaction can be as supportive as meeting in person.
senses.exampleCN: 线上社会互动能像当面相见一样给人支持。
senses.why: the phrase kept its shape while the channel changed: the action still passes between people, even when the space between them is digital.
senses.whyCN: 渠道变了而短语不变形：动作仍在人与人之间传递，即便两人之间的空间是数字的。

senses.title: Shared meanings built in encounter
senses.titleCN: 在往来中共同建构意义
senses.definition: the sociological view that meaning, identity and social order are produced and repaired in everyday dealings
senses.definitionCN: 社会学观点：意义、身份与秩序在日常往来中被生产与修补
senses.example: Sociologists study how social interaction builds shared meanings that no single person owns.
senses.exampleCN: 社会学家研究社会互动如何建构出并非任何个人独有的共同意义。
senses.why: this sense extends the reciprocal-action core into a theory: if every response adjusts to the last, then meanings are jointly made rather than privately held.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项把「相互动作」的核心扩展为理论：若每次回应都调整向前一次，那么意义就是共同造出的，而非私人持有的。

senses.title: Contact across group boundaries
senses.definition: dealings between people of different languages, classes or communities
senses.definitionCN: 不同语言、阶层或社群的人之间的往来
senses.example: Festivals create social interaction across language boundaries.
senses.exampleCN: 节庆活动造出跨越语言界限的社会互动。
senses.why: the phrase can be scaled up from two persons to whole groups, because the same back-and-forth pattern appears between collectives.
senses.whyCN: 短语可从两个人放大到整个群体，因为同样的来回模式也出现在集体之间。

senses.title: Coordination and unwritten rules
senses.titleCN: 互动中的协调与不成文规矩
senses.definition: the subtle cues, timing and politeness that keep an exchange smooth or make it fail
senses.definitionCN: 使交流顺畅或失败的那些细微线索、时机与礼貌
senses.example: Daily social interaction depends on subtle cues such as timing and gaze.
senses.exampleCN: 社会互动依赖时机与目光这类细微线索。
senses.why: the prefix 'between' implies two sides that must stay in step, and that requirement for mutual adjustment is what the rules of interaction formalise.
senses.whyCN: 表示「在……之间」的前缀意味着两侧必须同步，而相互调适的要求正是互动规则所形式化的东西。

intro.en: Social comes from Latin socialis, from socius 'companion, ally'. Interaction comes from inter- 'between' plus agere 'to do, to drive', whose past participle stem act- gives action; the noun therefore means action that runs between two parties. The fixed phrase took shape in twentieth-century sociology. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: social 出自拉丁 socialis，源于 socius「同伴、盟友」。interaction 出自表示「在……之间」的拉丁前缀加 agere「做、驱动」，其过去分词提供的词干又构成表示「行动」的名词，因此本义是「在两者之间来回动作」。这个固定短语在二十世纪社会学中定型。年代均为约数。

items.en: Socius 'companion, ally' gave socialis 'of companions, of a community', which English shortened to social.
items.cn: socius「同伴、盟友」给出 socialis「同伴的、共同体的」，英语截取为 social。

items.en: Agere meant 'to do, to drive, to set in motion'; its past participle actus supplied the stem act- used in nouns of action.
items.cn: agere 意为「做、驱动、使动」，其过去分词提供名词中所用的动作词干。

items.en: The prefix inter- 'between' combined with the action stem produced a noun for action passing between parties, recorded in English from the early eighteenth century.
items.cn: 表示「在……之间」的前缀与动作词干结合，造出「在双方之间传递的动作」这一名词，英语自十八世纪初有记录。

items.en: English formed interaction from the prefix and the noun action, and the verb interact was later back-formed from it.
items.cn: 英语用该前缀与表示「行动」的名词造出表示「互动」的名词，动词形式则是后来由它逆构而成。

items.en: Sociology adopted the phrase in the twentieth century to name the basic unit of everyday life, the exchange between two or more people.
items.cn: 社会学在二十世纪采用这一短语，用来指日常生活的基本单位，即两个或更多人之间的往来。

items.en: From the late twentieth century the phrase extended to mediated and online contact without changing its core of reciprocal action.
items.cn: 二十世纪后期起，这个短语扩展到经由媒介与线上的接触，而其「相互动作」的核心未变。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same action stock that are routinely mixed up; group two holds terms for people dealing with one another, each narrower or wider than the phrase.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「动作」词族、常被混用的词；第二组是关于人们彼此打交道的术语，各自比这个短语更窄或更宽。

entries.definition: The noun without the social label; it also covers drugs, particles and systems, so it is broader than the phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 不带「社会」限定的名词，也覆盖药物、粒子与系统，因此比该短语更宽。

entries.definition: The verb back-formed from the noun; it names the doing, while the phrase names the process as a topic of study.
entries.definitionCN: 由名词逆构而成的动词，指「去做」这个动作；短语则把该过程当作研究对象。

entries.definition: Describes something that responds to a user, such as software; it is a property, not an event between people.
entries.definitionCN: 描述能对使用者作出反应的事物，如软件；它是一种属性，不是人与人之间的事件。

entries.definition: The trait of enjoying company; the phrase names actual dealings, not the taste for them.
entries.definitionCN: 喜欢与人相处的性情；短语指实际的往来，而非对这种往来的喜好。

entries.definition: The passing of information or feeling; it can be one-way, while interaction requires response.
entries.definitionCN: 信息或情感的传递；它可以单向，而互动要求有回应。

entries.definition: The state of being in touch with someone; it may be minimal, whereas interaction implies repeated exchange.
entries.definitionCN: 与某人保持接触的状态；可以极为有限，而互动意味着反复交换。

entries.definition: Active involvement with people or a task; it stresses commitment of attention rather than reciprocity.
entries.definitionCN: 对人主动投入；强调注意力的投入，而非相互回应。

entries.definition: An older word for dealings between people or nations; it survives mainly in formal and historical writing.
entries.definitionCN: 指人或国家间往来的旧词，如今主要用于正式与历史文本。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin steps behind both halves, the real derived family, and the real settings in which the phrase is used.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想取自两半背后真实的拉丁演变、真实的派生词族，以及这个短语被使用的真实场景。

normal.en: socius 'companion' gives social: the parties who face each other.
normal.cn: socius「同伴」给出 social：彼此面对的那两方。

normal.en: inter- 'between' plus agere 'do': action running back and forth between two sides.
normal.cn: 表示「在……之间」的前缀加 agere「做」：动作在两侧之间来回跑。

normal.en: The family runs interact, interaction, interactive, interactivity and social.
normal.cn: 词族包括 interact、interaction、interactive、interactivity 与 social。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the research sense: face-to-face social interaction, patterns of social interaction, online social interaction.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出研究义：面对面社会互动、社会互动模式、线上社会互动。

normal.en: The countability is real and useful: one interaction can be counted, but interaction as a process cannot.
normal.cn: 可数性确有其用：一次互动可以计数，而作为过程的互动则不可数。

abstract.en: Picture two hands passing a cup back and forth across a table.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手在桌面上来回传递一只杯子。

abstract.en: Picture two people stepping in time because neither will move before the other.
abstract.cn: 想象两个人同步迈步，因为谁也不肯先于对方动。

abstract.en: Picture a conversation where every answer is already shaped by the question before it.
abstract.cn: 想象一场谈话，每个回答都已被前一个问题塑过形。

examples.en: Everyday social interaction in the market keeps neighbours informed and ties them together.
examples.cn: 市场里的日常社会互动让邻里互通消息、彼此联结。

examples.en: Online social interaction can be as supportive as meeting in person.
examples.cn: 线上社会互动能像当面相见一样给人支持。

examples.en: The study coded every social interaction in the classroom by speaker turn.
examples.cn: 这项研究按发言轮次对教室里的每一次社会互动进行编码。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「social（同伴）+ interaction（你来我往）」——同伴之间一来一往 → 社会互动

root: 拉丁 socius「同伴」→ socialis → social；拉丁表示「在……之间」的前缀 + agere「做、驱动」，其过去分词提供的词干构成表示「行动」的名词，合成表示「互动」的名词；二十世纪社会学中与 social 合为固定短语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses unroll from one motion: action passes between two sides, is cut into single encounters, repeats into a pattern, settles into turn-taking, moves onto screens, becomes the place where meaning is made, scales up to groups, and finally reveals the rules that keep the whole motion smooth.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项由同一个动作展开：动作在两侧之间传递，被切成单次接触，反复成格局，落成话轮，移上屏幕，成为意义生成之处，再放大到群体，最后显出维持整个过程顺畅的规则。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cup passing back and forth across a table, neither hand letting go for long.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只杯子在桌面上来回传递，两只手都不久握不放。

branches.en: THE BASIC MOTION: reciprocal action as a process, and one bounded episode of it.
branches.cn: 基本动作：作为过程的相互动作，以及其中一次有始有终的片段。

branches.en: REPETITION AND RHYTHM: repeated episodes harden into a pattern, and the pattern is lived out in turn-taking.
branches.cn: 重复与节奏：反复的片段硬化为格局，而格局就在轮流发言中被实际活出来。

branches.en: SCREEN AND MEANING: the same motion moves online, and in sociology it becomes the workshop where shared meaning is built.
branches.cn: 屏幕与意义：同一动作移往线上，并在社会学中成为共同意义被制造的工坊。

branches.en: SCALE: the pattern repeats between groups, not only between two persons.
branches.cn: 尺度：这一模式不只在两人之间，也在群体之间重现。

branches.en: RULES: timing, gaze and politeness are the grease that keeps the back-and-forth from jamming.
branches.cn: 规则：时机、目光与礼貌是润滑剂，使来回传递不致卡死。

intro.en: The phrase splits cleanly: social from a Latin noun for a companion, and interaction from a prefix meaning 'between' plus a verb of doing.
intro.cn: 这个短语可以干净地拆开：social 来自拉丁语表示「同伴」的名词，interaction 来自表示「在……之间」的前缀加一个表示「做」的动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin socius and socialis stand behind social; Latin inter- and agere, with its participle stem act-, stand behind interaction.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 socius 与 socialis 是 social 的来源；拉丁表示「在……之间」的前缀与 agere 及其分词词干是 interaction 的来源。

items.example: The stem supplies the social half of the phrase.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干提供短语中「社会」的一半。

items.example: The suffix turns the noun for a companion into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把表示同伴的名词变成形容词。

items.example: Social ties set the stage for the exchange.
items.exampleCN: 社会关系为这种往来搭好台子。

items.example: The prefix makes the action run between two sides.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀使动作在两侧之间运行。

items.meaning: to do, drive, set in motion
items.example: The verb supplies the acting inside interaction.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词为 interaction 提供「动作」。

items.example: The stem appears in action and in the noun of interaction.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干出现在表示「行动」的名词中。

items.structure: suffix forming nouns of action or result
items.example: The suffix yields interaction from the action stem.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀由动作词干造出表示「互动」的名词。

items.meaningCN: 在双方之间传递的动作
items.example: The noun entered English in the early eighteenth century.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词于十八世纪初进入英语。

items.meaning: tending to, having the nature of
items.example: The suffix yields interactive, said of software that answers back.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀造出表示「能回应使用者」的形容词。

items.example: The suffix yields interactivity, the quality of responding.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀造出表示「互动性」的名词。

definition_zh: 跨骑；骑跨于；横跨；主宰；高踞……之上
definition_en: to sit or stand with a leg on each side of something; to dominate
core_image: 巨人叉腿跨立在河上，两岸尽在他脚下
scene: 桥还没修好，牧民只能跨马过溪。 The cowboy bestrode his horse with easy confidence.
sceneCN: 这里 bestride 是「跨骑」（第 1 个义项：两腿分跨两侧骑坐）；句意是牛仔自信地跨骑在马上。

derivatives.zh: 基础词，义为「大步走」，bestride 由其构成
近义动词，义为「跨坐；跨越」，与 stride 同源于古英语 strīdan
a- 加 stride，义为「跨着；两腿分开着」

senses.title: To sit with a leg on each side
senses.definition: to sit on something with one leg on either side, as on a horse
senses.definitionCN: 两腿分跨两侧地坐于其上，如骑马
senses.example: The cowboy bestrode his horse with easy confidence.
senses.exampleCN: 牛仔自信地跨骑在马上。
senses.why: The prefix be- plus stride pictures the legs spread in a stride across the mount.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 be- 加 stride，画出双腿如跨步般分开骑坐的画面。

senses.title: To stand over spanning something
senses.definition: to stand or extend over something from side to side
senses.definitionCN: 跨立于某物之上，两端各达一侧
senses.example: A stone bridge bestrode the narrow gorge.
senses.exampleCN: 一座石桥横跨在狭窄的峡谷上。
senses.why: The riding image widens to anything that stretches across a gap.
senses.whyCN: 骑跨的画面推广到任何横越空隙之物。

senses.title: To dominate lordly
senses.definition: to dominate or lord over something as if towering above it
senses.definitionCN: 如高踞其上般支配、称雄于某领域
senses.example: He bestrode the business world for three decades.
senses.exampleCN: 他主宰商界长达三十年。
senses.why: One who sits astride a thing holds it under him, hence mastery.
senses.whyCN: 跨骑者凌驾其上，故引申出支配之义。

senses.title: To span two things at once
senses.definition: to occupy a position connecting two different sides or fields
senses.definitionCN: 处于连接两个不同阵营或领域的位置
senses.example: The writer bestrides Eastern and Western traditions.
senses.exampleCN: 这位作家兼跨东西方传统。
senses.why: Spanning a bridge physically becomes spanning two worlds figuratively.
senses.whyCN: 物理上横跨桥梁，比喻上横跨两个世界。

senses.title: To get astride for control
senses.definition: to mount or get upon something in order to master it
senses.definitionCN: 跃上某物以便驾驭它
senses.example: The young chief bestrode the wild stallion at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 年轻的酋长清晨跃上那匹野马。
senses.why: Mounting is the first act of taming, so control begins by bestriding.
senses.whyCN: 跨上是驯服的第一步，控制始于骑跨。

senses.title: To stride across grandly (literary)
senses.titleCN: 昂然阔步跨越（文学用法）
senses.definition: to walk across something with proud, long strides
senses.definitionCN: 以骄傲的大步跨越而过（文学化用法）
senses.example: The giant bestrode the battlefield in the old tale.
senses.exampleCN: 在古老传说中，巨人昂然跨越战场。
senses.why: The stride root keeps its sense of long, powerful steps.
senses.whyCN: 词基 stride 保留了跨大步的力量感。

senses.title: To cover a range (of things)
senses.definition: to extend over or cover a whole range, as of dates or topics
senses.definitionCN: 延展覆盖一整段范围，如年代或话题
senses.example: Her research bestrides physics and philosophy.
senses.exampleCN: 她的研究横跨物理学与哲学。
senses.why: Fields, like rivers, can be spanned from end to end.
senses.whyCN: 领域如河流，也可自一头跨越到另一头。

senses.title: To sit firmly upon (of authority)
senses.definition: to sit securely upon a position of power
senses.definitionCN: 稳稳地坐在权力位置之上
senses.example: The old dynasty still bestrides the institution's rituals.
senses.exampleCN: 旧王朝依然稳踞于该机构的仪式之上。
senses.why: The rider's firm seat images secure, unshaken authority.
senses.whyCN: 骑手的稳坐象征稳固不移的权威。

intro.en: Bestride is the prefix be- plus stride, to step violently.
intro.cn: bestride 由前缀 be- 加 stride「跨步」构成。

items.en: the root streidh- meant to stride, to strive; reconstructed form.
items.cn: 词根 streidh- 意为「跨步、奋力」（重构形式）。

items.en: strīdan meant to stride, to mount with the legs apart.
items.cn: 古英语 strīdan 意为「跨步、叉腿骑上」。

items.en: bestrīdan meant to bestride, to get astride.
items.cn: 古英语 bestrīdan 意为「跨骑、骑上」。

items.en: bestriden kept the riding sense and grew a figurative sense of domination.
items.cn: 中古英语 bestriden 保留骑跨义，并长出主宰的比喻义。

items.en: now chiefly literary: to span or dominate, as in Shakespeare's giant image.
items.cn: 如今主要用于文学：横跨或主宰，如莎士比亚巨人的名句。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the stride root; the near-meaning group gathers spanning and dominating words.
note.cn: 形近组共享 stride 词根；近义组汇集横跨、主宰类词。

entries.definition: to extend across from end to end

normalIntro.cn: bestride 是 be- 加 stride：双腿如跨步分开于两侧。

normal.en: The past is bestrode, participle bestridden.

normal.en: Astride is the adverb cousin.

normal.en: Shakespeare wrote of a giant bestriding the narrow world.

abstract.cn: 看巨人一脚踏一岸，横立大河之上。

abstract.en: Feel the saddle grip as you rise to ride.
abstract.cn: 感受跃上马背时鞍鞯的扣紧。

abstract.en: Picture a tycoon standing over the whole market map.
abstract.cn: 想象巨头俯立在整个市场版图之上。

examples.en: The cowboy bestrode his horse with easy confidence.
examples.cn: 牛仔自信地跨骑在马上。

examples.en: A stone bridge bestrode the narrow gorge.
examples.cn: 一座石桥横跨在狭窄的峡谷上。

examples.en: He bestrode the business world for three decades.

dict_mnemonic.text: 「必·撕踹」——必得把马两边撕开般叉腿跨上，狠狠踹蹬前行。

definition_zh: 增强现实；把数字内容实时叠加到实景画面上的技术；叠加后的观看体验
definition_en: a technology that lays computer-generated content over a live view of the real world
core_image: 一面断墙前举起平板，屏幕上沿着残存的石缝补出当年的拱顶与彩绘
scene: 导览员举起平板，镜头里的断墙上方自动叠出它当年的完整样貌。 Augmented reality restored the missing roof on the screen.
sceneCN: 这里指把数字内容叠加到实时画面上（第 1 个义项：在实景上叠加数字信息）；句意为增强现实在屏幕上补出了缺失的屋顶。图中可辨识物件：平板、断墙、叠加线框、护栏。

pos.zh: 增强现实；实景叠加数字内容的技术

senses.title: Digital content over a live view
senses.definition: computer-generated images, text or sound laid over what the camera or eye sees in real time
senses.definitionCN: 计算机生成的图像、文字或声音实时叠加在镜头或眼睛所见之上
senses.example: The app uses augmented reality to label the machine parts.
senses.exampleCN: 这个应用用增强现实给机器零件加标注。
senses.why: Augmented says the real view is kept and added to, while virtual reality replaces it altogether.
senses.whyCN: 「增强」表示真实视图被保留并加以增补，而虚拟现实把它整个替换。

senses.title: The technology and industry
senses.definition: the hardware, software and companies that build overlays on live views
senses.definitionCN: 在实景视图上构建叠加层的硬件、软件与公司
senses.example: Augmented reality is moving from phones into glasses.
senses.exampleCN: 增强现实正从手机转向眼镜。
senses.why: Once a technique has a name, the businesses around it take the same name.
senses.whyCN: 当一种技术有了名字，围绕它的生意也用同一个名字。

senses.title: An app or a game
senses.definition: a program that places characters or objects into the camera view of a device
senses.definitionCN: 把角色或物件放进设备镜头画面的程序
senses.example: The game's augmented reality mode sends players into the square.
senses.exampleCN: 这款游戏的增强现实模式把玩家送进广场。
senses.why: The consumer form of the technique is a piece of software you point at the street.
senses.whyCN: 这项技术的消费者形态，是一个可以对着街道举起来的软件。

senses.title: Retail try-on
senses.definition: the placing of a product image on a customer's body or room through a camera
senses.definitionCN: 通过镜头把产品图像放到顾客身上或房间里
senses.example: The furniture shop added augmented reality so buyers could see a chair at home.
senses.exampleCN: 家具店加入增强现实，让买家能把椅子看到家里。
senses.why: The overlay answers a practical question: how would this look here, before it is bought.
senses.whyCN: 叠加层回答一个实际问题：买之前，这东西放在这里会是什么样。

senses.title: Surgical and industrial guidance
senses.definition: the projection of scans, measurements or instructions onto the field a professional is working in
senses.definitionCN: 把扫描、测量或指示投射到专业人员正在操作的现场
senses.example: Surgeons used augmented reality to see the vessel under the skin.
senses.exampleCN: 外科医生用增强现实看见皮下的血管。
senses.why: When the overlay sits on the patient or the pipe, hidden structure becomes visible where it is needed.
senses.whyCN: 当叠加层落在病人或管道上，隐藏的结构就在需要的地方变得可见。

senses.title: Education and museums
senses.definition: the use of overlays to show what is absent, ruined or invisible at a site
senses.definitionCN: 用叠加层在现场展示缺失、残毁或不可见之物
senses.example: The museum's augmented reality rebuilt the fallen wall for visitors.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆的增强现实为参观者重建了倒塌的墙。
senses.why: The added layer is a memory attached to a real place, which is the gentlest use of the technology.
senses.whyCN: 被加上的一层是附在真实地点上的记忆，这是这项技术最温和的用法。

senses.title: Headsets and glasses
senses.definition: wearable see-through displays that add images to the wearer's ordinary field of view
senses.definitionCN: 在佩戴者平常视野中增添图像的可透视穿戴显示设备
senses.example: The new augmented reality glasses weigh less than a phone.
senses.exampleCN: 新的增强现实眼镜比一部手机还轻。
senses.why: The hardware branch names the device by what it adds, not by what it shows.
senses.whyCN: 硬件这一支以「增加什么」而非「显示什么」来命名设备。

senses.title: Mediated perception
senses.definition: a way of seeing in which what is present and what is added can no longer be easily separated
senses.definitionCN: 一种看见的方式，其中在场之物与添加之物已不易分开
senses.example: Critics describe social media as augmented reality for the ego.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者把社交媒体描述为给自我用的增强现实。
senses.why: The concept sense is the phrase at its widest: every screen adds a layer to what we call real.
senses.whyCN: 概念义是这个短语最宽的一层：每一块屏幕都给我们所谓的真实加上一层。

intro.en: Augmented reality joins augmented, from Latin augmentare 'to increase' and augere 'to grow', with reality, from Latin realis 'of a thing'. The term is generally attributed to Boeing researcher Tom Caudell around 1990; the exact first written use is source uncertain.
intro.cn: augmented reality 由 augmented（拉丁 augmentare「增加」、augere「生长」）与 reality（拉丁 realis「事物的」）组合。该术语一般认为由波音研究员汤姆·考德尔约一九九〇年提出；最早的书面用例来源不确定。

items.en: Latin augere meant to grow or increase, and gave augment, author and auction through related paths.
items.cn: 拉丁 augere 指生长或增加，经相关路径衍生 augment、author 与 auction。

items.en: Augmentare meant to make larger or to add to, and English augment keeps that plain sense of adding.
items.cn: augmentare 指使变大或增添，英语 augment 保留了「添加」这一直白意思。

items.en: Latin realis meant of a thing, from res 'thing', and reality names what is actually there.
items.cn: 拉丁 realis 指属于某物的，源自 res「事物」；reality 命名实际存在之物。

items.en: Boeing researcher Tom Caudell is generally credited with the term around 1990 for overlays that guided factory workers; the first written instance is source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为波音研究员汤姆·考德尔约一九九〇年为指导工人的叠加显示提出该术语；最早的书面实例来源不确定。

items.en: The 1990s saw overlays on assembly lines and in military displays, where instructions could sit on the object itself.
items.cn: 二十世纪九十年代，叠加层出现在装配线与军用显示器上，指示可以直接落在物件上。

items.en: Smartphones in the 2010s brought the technique to the public, and see-through glasses later moved it from the hand to the face.
items.cn: 二十一世纪一十年代的智能手机把这项技术带给大众，可透视眼镜后来把它从手上移到眼前。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like augmented reality; the second group names neighbouring ideas in the same field.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与「augmented reality」相近；第二组是同一领域里意思相邻的其他说法。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to add to or increase something.
entries.definitionCN: 指增加或增补某物的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for an addition or the act of adding.
entries.definitionCN: 表示增添或增添行为的名称。

entries.definition: The participle used in the phrase, meaning increased by an added layer.
entries.definitionCN: 短语中使用的分词，意为被添加的一层所增强。

entries.definition: The second element, naming the real world that is added to.
entries.definitionCN: 第二部分，命名被添加的真实世界。

entries.definition: A reasoned case or a quarrel; it looks close but comes from a different Latin verb.
entries.definitionCN: 论证或争吵；形近，却来自另一个拉丁动词。

entries.definition: A generated world that replaces the real view instead of adding to it.
entries.definitionCN: 取代而非增补真实视图的生成世界。

entries.definition: A space where real and generated objects interact rather than merely overlap.
entries.definitionCN: 真实与生成之物相互作用、而非仅叠加的空间。

entries.definition: A layer placed on top of another image.
entries.definitionCN: 放在另一图像之上的一层。

entries.definition: The process by which a device or medium stands between a person and the world.
entries.definitionCN: 设备或媒介挡在人与世界之间的过程。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin growth word, the real dated history and real product phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实拉丁「增长」词、真实可考年代与真实产品搭配。

normal.en: Augere is Latin for grow, so augmented reality is reality with something grown onto it.
normal.cn: augere 是拉丁语「生长」，因此增强现实就是长出了一层的现实。

normal.en: The family runs augment, augmentation, augmented and the fixed phrase augmented reality.
normal.cn: 同族词有 augment、augmentation、augmented 与固定短语 augmented reality。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: app, glasses, display, navigation, try-on.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出用法：应用、眼镜、显示、导航、试穿。

normal.en: The abbreviation AR is common in shops, schools and research.
normal.cn: 缩写 AR 在商店、学校与研究中通用。

normal.en: Virtual reality replaces the view; augmented reality keeps it and adds a layer.
normal.cn: 虚拟现实替换视图；增强现实保留视图并加一层。

abstract.en: The added layer sits on the object like a note stuck to it.
abstract.cn: 添加的那一层像一张便签贴在物件上。

abstract.en: The real wall remains; only the missing roof is drawn in.
abstract.cn: 真实的墙还在，只把缺失的屋顶画了上去。

abstract.en: When the layer is good enough, the eye stops asking which part is drawn.
abstract.cn: 当这一层足够好，眼睛就不再追问哪部分是被画出来的。

examples.en: Augmented reality turned the empty square into a guide to its own history.
examples.cn: 增强现实把空荡的广场变成了它自身历史的向导。

examples.en: The app uses augmented reality to show how the sofa would fit the room.
examples.cn: 这个应用用增强现实展示沙发如何放进房间。

examples.en: Engineers wore augmented reality glasses while repairing the turbine.
examples.cn: 工程师修理涡轮时戴着增强现实眼镜。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「增强 + 现实」——现实没被换掉，只被加上一层看得见的信息

root: augmented 来自拉丁 augere「生长、增加」，经 augmentare「使增大」；reality 来自拉丁 realis「事物的」、res「事物」。术语一般认为由波音的考德尔约一九九〇年提出，最早书面用例来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one added layer: a live view with digital content, an industry, an app, a try-on, a surgical guide, a museum reconstruction, a pair of glasses, and a mediated way of seeing.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着同一层添加物：带数字内容的实时视图、一个产业、一个应用、一次试穿、一次手术引导、一次博物馆重建、一副眼镜，以及一种被中介的观看方式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tablet held before a broken wall redraws the missing roof exactly where it stood.
core.cn: 核心意象：一面断墙前举起平板，缺失的屋顶被画回它原来的位置。

branches.en: THE LAYER AND THE GLASS: content is laid over the live view, first on a held screen and later on the face.
branches.cn: 层与眼镜：内容叠加在实时视图上，先是在举起的屏幕上，后来在眼前。

branches.en: THE TRADE AND THE TOY: the technique becomes an industry and a game you point at the street.
branches.cn: 行业与玩物：技术变成产业，也变成对着街道举起的游戏。

branches.en: THE PRACTICAL QUESTION: will this chair look right here, asked before the purchase.
branches.cn: 实际问题：这把椅子放在这里好看吗，在购买之前就问。

branches.en: THE HIDDEN AND THE LOST: a vessel under the skin and a roof that fell are both drawn back into place.
branches.cn: 隐藏与失去：皮下的血管与倒塌的屋顶都被画回原位。

branches.en: THE WIDEST SENSE: every screen adds a layer to what we agree to call real.
branches.cn: 最宽的一层：每一块屏幕都给我们公认的真实加上一层。

intro.en: Augmented reality joins the Latin growth word augere with the Latin thing word res.
intro.cn: augmented reality 把拉丁「生长」词 augere 与拉丁「事物」词 res 连在一起。

latinIntro.en: Latin augere gives augmentare and English augment; Latin res gives realis and English reality; English joins the participles into a fixed term.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 augere 衍生 augmentare 与英语 augment；拉丁 res 衍生 realis 与英语 reality；英语把两个分词连成固定术语。

definition_zh: 食虫动物；以昆虫为主食的动物（也指食虫植物）
definition_en: an animal or plant that feeds chiefly on insects
core_image: 一只小兽扒开朽木，专挑里面的虫子吃
scene: 这里指「食虫动物」。 A shrew is a true insectivore that hunts beetles and grubs in the leaf litter.
sceneCN: 这里 insectivore 是「食虫动物」（第 1 个义项：以昆虫为主食的动物）；句意：鼩鼱是真正的食虫动物，在落叶层中捕食甲虫和蛴螬。

pos.zh: 食虫动物；食虫生物；食虫植物（可数，复数 insectivores）

senses.title: An animal that lives on insects
senses.definition: an animal whose diet consists mainly of insects
senses.definitionCN: 以昆虫为主要食物的动物
senses.example: Shrews and moles are insectivores that seldom surface above the litter.
senses.exampleCN: 鼩鼱和鼹鼠是食虫动物，很少爬到落叶层以上活动。
senses.why: The word joins Latin for insect with a Latin root meaning to devour, so it names a feeder purely by what it eats.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把拉丁语的「昆虫」与表示「吞食」的词根连在一起，完全按「吃什么」来给取食者命名。

senses.title: A member of an old mammal order
senses.definition: a mammal formerly placed in the order Insectivora, such as a shrew, a mole or a hedgehog
senses.definitionCN: 曾被归入食虫目的哺乳动物，如鼩鼱、鼹鼠或刺猬
senses.example: The hedgehog was long treated as a typical insectivore by taxonomists.
senses.exampleCN: 刺猬长期被分类学家当作典型的食虫目动物。
senses.why: Nineteenth-century zoology needed a label for mammals grouped by an insect diet, and it simply reused the everyday word as an order name.
senses.whyCN: 19 世纪的动物学需要给「按食虫习性归为一类」的哺乳动物一个名称，于是直接把这个日常词升格为目名。

senses.title: A plant that traps insects
senses.definition: a plant that captures and digests insects to obtain nutrients
senses.definitionCN: 捕捉并消化昆虫以获取养分的植物
senses.example: The sundew is an insectivore that supplements poor soil with trapped midges.
senses.exampleCN: 茅膏菜是一种食虫植物，用捕获的蠓虫弥补贫瘠土壤的养分。
senses.why: Botany extended the eater-and-food relation to plants, keeping the insect as the food and the plant as the consumer.
senses.whyCN: 植物学把「吃与被吃」的关系套用到植物身上，昆虫仍是食物，植物成了取食一方。

senses.title: Any predator of insects
senses.definition: broadly, any bird, reptile, amphibian or fish whose prey is largely insects
senses.definitionCN: 泛指以昆虫为主要猎物的鸟类、爬行类、两栖类或鱼类
senses.example: Many songbirds are insectivores during the breeding season.
senses.exampleCN: 许多鸣禽在繁殖季都是食虫动物。
senses.why: Once the label means insect-eater, it can describe any predator whose prey is mostly insects, not only the mammals of the old order.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词的意思是「吃昆虫的」，它就能描述任何以昆虫为主的捕食者，而不限于旧目里的哺乳动物。

senses.title: A role in the food web
senses.definition: an organism assigned to the insect-eating functional group in community ecology
senses.definitionCN: 群落生态学中归入「食虫」功能群的生物
senses.example: The study compared insectivores and granivores across the same grassland.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究在同一片草地上比较了食虫动物与食种子动物。
senses.why: Ecology classifies organisms by what they do rather than what they are, so the old dietary noun became the name of a functional guild.
senses.whyCN: 生态学按「做什么」而不是「是什么」来分类，于是这个古老的「食性名词」变成了功能群的名称。

senses.title: A person who eats insects
senses.definition: a person whose diet regularly includes insects, especially in entomophagy research
senses.definitionCN: 日常饮食中包含昆虫的人，常见于食虫研究语境
senses.example: The survey asked whether local insectivores preferred roasted or boiled larvae.
senses.exampleCN: 这项调查询问当地的食虫者更喜欢烤的还是煮的幼虫。
senses.why: The same eater-and-food pattern applies to humans, though the word is far rarer here than the dietary term entomophagy.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「吃与被吃」模式也适用于人，不过在这个意义上，这个词远不如表示「食虫」的 entomophagy 常用。

senses.title: A natural pest controller
senses.definition: an insect-eating species valued in agriculture for suppressing pests
senses.definitionCN: 在农业上因抑制害虫而受重视的食虫物种
senses.example: Farmers installed bat boxes because the insectivores cut moth numbers sharply.
senses.exampleCN: 农民挂起蝙蝠箱，因为这些食虫动物大幅减少了蛾的数量。
senses.why: Conservation writing shifts from what the animal eats to what that eating does for people, turning the eater into a service provider.
senses.whyCN: 保护类写作把重点从「它吃什么」转到「这种吃对人有什么用」，于是取食者变成了服务的提供者。

senses.title: An insect-eater in the fossil record
senses.definition: a fossil species reconstructed as insect-eating from its teeth or gut contents
senses.definitionCN: 依据牙齿或胃肠内容物推断为食虫的化石物种
senses.example: Paleontologists identified the tiny jaw as an insectivore from its sharp molars.
senses.exampleCN: 古生物学家根据其锋利的臼齿，把这枚小颌骨鉴定为食虫类。
senses.why: Paleontology infers diet from anatomy, so the same word marks a reconstructed feeding habit rather than an observed one.
senses.whyCN: 古生物学依据解剖结构推断食性，因此这个词标记的是重建出来的取食习惯，而不是直接观察到的行为。

intro.en: Insectivore is a scientific compound of a Latin noun for insect and a Latin root meaning to devour.
intro.cn: insectivore 是一个科学复合词，由拉丁语「昆虫」名词与表示「吞食」的拉丁词根构成。

items.en: Insect goes back to Latin insectum, literally 'a thing cut into', from insecare (in- 'into' + secare 'to cut'). It was a loan-translation of Greek entomon, which also meant 'cut in two'.
items.cn: insect 上溯至拉丁语 insectum，字面是「被切开的东西」，来自 insecare（in-「进入」+ secare「切」）。它是对希腊语 entomon 的仿译，而 entomon 同样有「切成两段」之意。

items.en: The second element comes from Latin vorare, 'to devour, swallow whole', the source of voracious and of the -vore ending in carnivore and herbivore.
items.cn: 第二个成分来自拉丁语 vorare「吞食、整口吞下」，也是 voracious 以及 carnivore、herbivore 中 -vore 词尾的来源。

items.en: French insectivore and scientific Latin Insectivora brought the two elements together in the early nineteenth century. The connecting -i- belongs to the Latin stem, not to English word formation.
items.cn: 法语 insectivore 与科学拉丁语 Insectivora 在 19 世纪初把两个成分组合起来。连接元音 -i- 来自拉丁词干，而不是英语自身的构词习惯。

items.en: Insectivora was a mammalian order covering shrews, moles and hedgehogs. Molecular studies showed the group was not a single lineage, so the order has been abandoned, though the everyday word survives.
items.cn: Insectivora 曾是一个哺乳动物目，包含鼩鼱、鼹鼠与刺猬。分子研究显示这一群体并非单一谱系，因此该目已被废弃，但日常用词仍然保留。

items.en: From the mid-nineteenth century the word also named insect-catching plants; Darwin's book on insectivorous plants in 1875 fixed the usage in English.
items.cn: 自 19 世纪中叶起，这个词也用来指捕虫植物；达尔文 1875 年关于食虫植物的著作使这一用法在英语中固定下来。

note.en: The first group holds words built from the same elements; the second holds words for other feeding types.
note.cn: 第一组是用相同构词成分造出的词；第二组是表示其他食性的词。

entries.definition: Describes an animal or plant with that diet; insectivore is the creature itself.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，描述具有这种食性的动物或植物；insectivore 指生物本身。

entries.definition: Names the habit or diet itself, so it cannot stand for a shrew or a sundew.
entries.definitionCN: 指食虫的习性饮食本身，不能用来指鼩鼱或茅膏菜这类生物。

entries.definition: The prey; it carries no information about who eats it.
entries.definitionCN: 指被捕食的昆虫，本身不包含「谁来吃」的信息。

entries.definition: An animal that feeds on detritus, the dead and decaying fragments of organisms; the food differs, the eating pattern matches.
entries.definitionCN: 指以腐屑为食的动物，腐屑是生物死亡后破碎的残余；食物不同，但取食模式相同。

entries.definition: An animal that eats other animals, insects included; insectivore is the narrower, diet-specific term.
entries.definitionCN: 指吃其他动物的动物，昆虫也在其中；insectivore 范围更窄，专指食虫。

entries.definition: An animal that eats both plant and animal matter; an insectivore may take the occasional plant, but insects dominate.
entries.definitionCN: 指动植物都吃的动物；食虫动物偶尔也吃植物，但以昆虫为主。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real relatives and real collocations.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的同族词与真实搭配。

normal.en: insect + -vore 'devourer': an insect-devourer.
normal.cn: insect「昆虫」+ -vore「吞食者」：吞食昆虫者。

normal.en: The family runs insectivore, insectivorous, insectivory and insect.
normal.cn: 同族词有 insectivore、insectivorous、insectivory、insect。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the technical senses: obligate insectivore, insectivore guild, insectivore species.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出技术义项：专性食虫动物、食虫功能群、食虫物种。

normal.en: A shrew in the leaf litter is the picture the word was made for.
normal.cn: 落叶层里的鼩鼱，就是这个词最初描绘的画面。

normal.en: The -vore ending recurs in carnivore, herbivore and omnivore, all naming eaters.
normal.cn: -vore 词尾在 carnivore、herbivore、omnivore 中反复出现，都表示「吃某物者」。

abstract.en: Picture a menu with only one item: insects. Whoever lives on that menu is an insectivore.
abstract.cn: 想象一份只有一道菜的菜单：昆虫。靠这份菜单过活的，就是食虫动物。

abstract.en: Think of a pest-control worker paid in protein instead of money.
abstract.cn: 把它想成一个用蛋白质而不是工资结算的害虫防治工。

abstract.en: A pitfall trap in the soil is the animal's pantry: whatever falls in is dinner.
abstract.cn: 土壤里的陷阱是这种动物的食品柜：掉进去什么，晚餐就是什么。

examples.en: Shrews are insectivores that must eat almost constantly to fuel their fast metabolism.
examples.cn: 鼩鼱是食虫动物，必须几乎不停地进食来支撑快速代谢。

examples.en: The fossil jaw suggests an insectivore about the size of a thumb.
examples.cn: 这块化石颌骨显示出一种只有拇指大小的食虫动物。

examples.en: Conservationists count insectivores among the best natural controls of crop pests.
examples.cn: 保护工作者把食虫动物列为农作物害虫最好的天然控制者之一。

dict_mnemonic.text: in（在……里）+ sect（切）+ vore（吞）→ 把虫子切开吞下去 → 食虫动物

root: 拉丁语 insectum「昆虫」（由 insecare「切开」而来，in- + secare「切」）+ 拉丁语 vorare「吞食」+ 名词后缀 -ore → insectivore，字面即「吞食昆虫者」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses grow from one relation: an eater and its insect food. Classification, botany, ecology, agriculture, human diet and paleontology each borrowed the word for their own version of that relation.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都从一个关系生长出来：取食者与它的昆虫食物。分类学、植物学、生态学、农业、人类饮食与古生物学各自借用了这个词，来描述自己版本的那层关系。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small hunter whose entire menu is insects.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个整份菜单只有昆虫的小型捕食者。

chain: A ROLE IN THE FOOD WEB

branches.en: THE CORE: a diet of insects defines the animal, and taxonomy once borrowed that definition as an order name.
branches.cn: 核心：昆虫食性定义了这类动物，分类学曾把这一界定借去当作目名。

branches.en: OTHER EATERS: plants and non-mammalian predators join the category whenever insects are their main food.
branches.cn: 其他取食者：只要昆虫是主要食物，植物和非哺乳类捕食者也能进入这一类别。

branches.en: THE ROLE: ecology ignores species and groups anything that eats insects into one functional guild.
branches.cn: 角色：生态学不看物种，只把所有吃昆虫的生物归入同一个功能群。

branches.en: THE HUMAN: people who eat insects are described by the same pattern, though a different technical term is usual.
branches.cn: 人类：吃昆虫的人也能套用同一模式，只是通常使用另一个专业术语。

branches.en: APPLIED VIEWS: agriculture sees a pest controller, paleontology sees a diet reconstructed from teeth.
branches.cn: 应用视角：农业看到的是害虫控制者，古生物学看到的是从牙齿重建出来的食性。

intro.en: Insectivore is a two-part scientific compound whose meaning is transparent from its Latin pieces.
intro.cn: insectivore 是一个两部分组成的科学复合词，其含义从拉丁语成分看一目了然。

latinIntro.en: Both parts are Latin: insectum for the prey and vorare for eating. The linking -i- is the stem vowel of insectum, and -ore marks the agent.
latinIntro.cn: 两部分都来自拉丁语：insectum 指猎物，vorare 指吞食。连接元音 -i- 是 insectum 的词干元音，-ore 标记施动者。

items.example: The hedgehog is a familiar insectivore of gardens.
items.exampleCN: 刺猬是花园里常见的食虫动物。

items.example: The insectivorous bird catches moths on the wing.
items.exampleCN: 这种食虫鸟在空中捕捉飞蛾。

items.example: Insectivory evolved independently in several mammal groups.
items.exampleCN: 食虫习性在多个哺乳动物类群中独立演化。

items.meaningCN: 六足的小型无脊椎动物
items.example: The bird searched the bark for insects.
items.exampleCN: 这只鸟在树皮上搜寻昆虫。

items.example: The orchard reduced insecticide use after planting hedgerows.
items.exampleCN: 果园在种下树篱后减少了杀虫剂的使用。

items.meaning: eating greedily and in large amounts
items.example: The larvae are voracious consumers of leaves.
items.exampleCN: 这些幼虫是叶子的贪婪取食者。

items.example: A carnivore of this size needs large prey.
items.exampleCN: 这个体型的食肉动物需要大型猎物。

items.example: The herbivore grazes between the shrubs.
items.exampleCN: 这种食草动物在灌木之间觅食。

latinEntries.meaning: an insect; literally 'a thing cut into'
latinEntries.meaningCN: 昆虫；字面为「被切开的东西」

definition_zh: 成为……的典型；概括；提炼
definition_en: to be a perfect example of something, or to state something in a very short form
core_image: 一座城市把所有时代的矛盾收进同一条街，走过这一条就算走完整座城
scene: 这条街浓缩了整座老城的心事。 This street epitomises the old town.
sceneCN: 这里 epitomise 是「成为……的典型；概括」（第 1 个义项：以一小段呈现整体）；句意：这条街是整座老城的缩影。

senses.title: To sum up a whole in one instance
senses.definition: to present an entire quality or class in a single clear example
senses.definitionCN: 用一个清晰的例子呈现整种性质或整类事物
senses.example: His silence epitomised the mood.
senses.exampleCN: 他的沉默正是那种心情的缩影。
senses.why: The Greek noun named an abstract copy, so one case could stand for the class.
senses.whyCN: 希腊名词指抽象的抄本，因此一个个例便可代表整类。

senses.title: To abridge a text
senses.definition: to restate a longer work in the fewest usable words
senses.definitionCN: 用最少的可用文字复述较长作品
senses.example: The editor epitomised the report.
senses.exampleCN: 编辑把报告压缩成摘要。
senses.why: Older rhetoric kept the abstracting sense that still lives in epitome.
senses.whyCN: 早期修辞学保留了摘要义，该义至今活在名词 epitome 里。

senses.title: To cut short
senses.definition: a rare use meaning to reduce a thing to its essentials
senses.definitionCN: 罕见用法，指把事物削减到仅剩精要
senses.example: Reform epitomised the committee.
senses.exampleCN: 改革把委员会缩减到最小规模。
senses.why: A literal sense from the Greek verb, to cut short, survives only on paper.
senses.whyCN: 来自希腊动词的字面义「切短」如今仅存于书面。

intro.en: Epitomise comes through Latin epitomizare from Greek epitomizein, to make an abstract, from epitome, an abridgement.
intro.cn: epitomise 经拉丁语 epitomizare 而来，源自希腊语 epitomizein「作摘要」，其基础是 epitome「节略本」。

items.en: Temnein means to cut.
items.cn: temnein 意为切。

items.en: Epitome names a cutting short, then a summary.
items.cn: epitome 先指切短，再指摘要。

items.en: Epitoma and epitomizare carry the noun into scholarship.
items.cn: epitoma 与 epitomizare 把名词带进学术。

items.en: Epitomiser supplies the modern verb shape.
items.cn: epitomiser 提供现代动词形式。

items.en: English first records the verb in a learned tone.
items.cn: 十七世纪英语首见该动词，语气书面。

items.en: Review writing makes it the praise of a perfect example.
items.cn: 十九世纪书评把它变成对典型之例的赞美。

note.en: Group one holds the temnein cutting family; group two holds other verbs of typifying and condensing.
note.cn: 第一组是 temnein 这一表切割的词族；第二组是其他表典型化与浓缩的动词。

entries.definition: The summary, or the perfect example itself.
entries.definitionCN: 摘要，或典型范例本身。

entries.definition: A division cut in two, from the Greek temnein.
entries.definitionCN: 切成两半的分立，出自希腊语 temnein。

entries.definition: To dissect, built on the same verb of cutting.
entries.definitionCN: 剖解分析，基于同一表切割的动词。

entries.definition: Greek atomos means the indivisible, sharing temnein.
entries.definitionCN: 希腊语 atomos 指不可分，同出 temnein。

entries.definition: To be a regular instance of a type.
entries.definitionCN: 作为某种类型的常态实例。

entries.definition: To illustrate by a case, without claiming perfection.
entries.definitionCN: 举例说明，不宣称完美无缺。

entries.definition: The plain way to compress a whole into a few words.
entries.definitionCN: 把整体压成数语的朴素说法。

entries.definition: To put into a small compass, close to the abridging sense.
entries.definitionCN: 纳入小范围，接近节略之义。

normalIntro.en: Epitomise is the British spelling; the American form drops the s for a z.
normalIntro.cn: epitomise 是英式拼写，美式把 s 换成 z。

normal.en: Its object is an abstract: a mood, an era, a virtue.
normal.cn: 宾语多为抽象物：心情、时代、美德。

normal.en: Use the passive with in: the age was epitomised in one song.
normal.cn: 与 in 连用表被动：一个时代浓缩在一首歌里。

normal.en: Do not epitomise a person; epitomise what they stand for.
normal.cn: 不要说概括某人，要概括其所代表之物。

normal.en: Reviewers favour it, engineers rarely use it.
normal.cn: 书评人偏爱此词，工程写作少用。

normal.en: The noun epitome keeps the same two senses.
normal.cn: 名词 epitome 保留同样的两个义项。

abstract.en: Picture a single street holding every argument of a whole city.
abstract.cn: 想象一条街道容下一座城市的所有争执。

abstract.en: Imagine scissors cutting a thick book down to one page.
abstract.cn: 想象剪刀把一本厚书裁到只剩一页。

abstract.en: Think of one photograph that ends a long debate about an era.
abstract.cn: 想想一张照片便终结了关于一个时代的长辩。

examples.en: One gesture epitomised her whole method.
examples.cn: 一个动作概括了她的全部方法。

examples.en: The slogan epitomises decades of patient research.
examples.cn: 这句口号浓缩了数十年沉静的研究。

examples.en: Critics felt the film epitomised the decade's anxiety.
examples.cn: 批评者认为该片是十年不安的典型写照。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一劈题眉子」——一刀劈下只留下题目最上面那一道眉，所以 epitomise 是提炼、概括成典型；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 epi-（在上）＋ temnein（切）→ epitome（切短之物、摘要）→ 拉丁语 epitomizare → 法语 epitomiser → 英语 epitomise，核心义「一刀切到只剩精要」。

sensesIntro.en: The verb moves from standing as a perfect example, to abridging a text, to a bookish sense of cutting short.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个动词从充当典型范例，到节略文本，再到书卷气的截短之义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one cut leaves the smallest piece that still shows the whole.
core.cn: 核心意象：一刀切下，留下的最小一片仍能显出全貌。

branches.en: The chosen instance carries the class.
branches.cn: 所选个例承载整类。

branches.en: The text is trimmed to usable length.
branches.cn: 文本被修剪到可用长度。

branches.en: A literal cutting sense lingers in old prose.
branches.cn: 字面的切割义留在早期文本中。

branches.en: Both begin from the image of the blade.
branches.cn: 两者都从刀的意象出发。

branches.en: Both mean making a thing shorter on purpose.
branches.cn: 两者都指有意使对象变短。

intro.en: A prefix of position, a stem of cutting, and a verbal ending assemble the word.
intro.cn: 表位置的前缀、表切割的词干与动词词尾装配成本词。

latinIntro.en: Greek temnein is to cut, Latin sectare is to cut too, and tomus is a section.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 temnein 表切，拉丁语 sectare 亦表切，tomus 表章节。

items.example: Epi- marks the cut from above.
items.exampleCN: epi- 标示自上而下的切。

items.example: Temnein is the deep stem.
The same stem yields the noun.
The noun precedes the verb.
The ending forms the British verb.
Common in past-tense commentary.
items.exampleCN: 在评论性过去时中常见。

definition_zh: vt. 给予…选举权；解放；使摆脱法律束缚
definition_en: to give a person or group the right to vote in elections, or to free someone from slavery or legal restraint
core_image: 登记处把新名字用墨水写进选民册，前一天还在服劳役的人在栏位上按下手印
scene: 改革法生效那天，登记处排起长队，职员逐个写下名字。 The reform act enfranchised thousands of former servants.
sceneCN: 这里 enfranchise 指「给予…选举权」（第 1 个义项：赋予投票的权利）；句意是改革法使数千名前仆役获得了选举权。

pos.zh: 给予…选举权；解放；使摆脱法律束缚

collocations.zh: 让一座自治市获得参政权

senses.title: To give the vote
senses.definition: to give a person or group the right to vote
senses.definitionCN: （动词）给予个人或群体投票的权利
senses.example: The reform act enfranchised thousands of former servants.
senses.exampleCN: 改革法使数千名前仆役获得了选举权。
senses.why: A clerk writing a new name into the voters roll in ink
senses.whyCN: 书记员用墨水把一个新名字写进选民册

senses.title: To free from servitude
senses.definition: to release someone from slavery or legal disability
senses.definitionCN: （动词）把人从奴隶身份或法律限制中释放出来
senses.example: The constitution enfranchised the freedmen at once.
senses.exampleCN: 宪法立即让获得自由的人享有完整权利。
senses.why: A chain lying open on a courthouse step beside a release paper
senses.whyCN: 法院台阶上一副摊开的锁链，旁边是释放文书

senses.title: To grant civic privileges
senses.titleCN: 授予市民特权；使获得自治权（历史）
senses.definition: to admit a town or a person to the privileges of citizenship
senses.definitionCN: （动词）让城镇或个人获得市民的特权
senses.example: The charter enfranchised the merchants of the town.
senses.exampleCN: 王室特许状让城中商人获得了市民特权。
senses.why: A guild seal pressed into wax on a town charter
senses.whyCN: 城市特许状上压进蜡里的行会印章

intro.en: Enfranchise is en- plus franchise, from Old French franc, free; the name of the Franks became the word for a free man, so to enfranchise is to make someone free in law.
intro.cn: enfranchise 由 en- 加 franchise 构成，franchise 出自意为自由的古法语 franc；指法兰克人的族名变成了指自由人的词，所以 enfranchise 就是使人在法律上成为自由人。

items.en: Francus names a member of the Frankish people.
items.cn: francus 指法兰克人中的一员。

items.en: Franc came to mean free, first of a Frank.
items.cn: franc 后来意为自由，最初只指法兰克人。

items.en: Franchise means the status and privileges of a free man.
items.cn: franchise 指自由人的身份与特权。

items.en: The verb enters English for admitting persons to privileges.
items.cn: 16 世纪该动词进入英语，指授予特权。

items.en: British reform acts enfranchise new groups of voters.
items.cn: 19 世纪英国改革法使新的选民群体获得选举权。

items.en: Franchise shifts to licensing, still a granted right.
items.cn: franchise 转入商业授权，仍是「被授予的权利」。

note.cn: enfranchise、franchise 与 enfranchisement 都建立在意为自由的古法语 franc 之上；franchise 的商业义同样从「被授予的特权」这一概念长出。

dict_mnemonic.text: enfranchise ＝ en-（使…）＋ franchise（自由身份；特权；选举权）＝「使人获得自由的权利」。franchise 出自意为自由的古法语 franc，本义是法兰克人，因为只有他们才是自由人。名词 enfranchisement 给予选举权与解放，franchisee 是被授权经营的人。三类用法：给投票权 enfranchise women、解放 enfranchise former slaves、授予市民特权 enfranchise a borough。与 emancipate 相比，这个词只看权利，不看身份解放的过程。
