definition_zh: 运动的；由运动产生的；动能的；动态的
definition_en: relating to, caused by, or producing motion
core_image: 台球桌上，一颗静止的球被另一颗撞开，滑过绿呢台面，力在相触的一瞬传了过去
scene: 台球桌上，一颗静止的球被另一颗撞开，滑过绿呢台面，力在相触的一瞬传了过去。 The kinetic energy of the moving ball is passed on the moment they touch.
sceneCN: 这里 kinetic 指与运动有关的（第 1 个义项：属于或关于运动）；句意：运动球体的动能就在两球相触的一瞬传了过去。图中可辨识物件：绿呢台面、两颗球、球杆、袋口。

pos.zh: 运动的；由运动产生的；动力学的

derivatives.zh: 在运动方面；从运动角度

senses.title: Relating to motion
senses.definition: relating to or involving movement
senses.definitionCN: 与移动、运动有关的
senses.example: Kinetic energy grows with the square of the speed.
senses.exampleCN: 动能随速度的平方增长。
senses.why: kinetic is simply the adjective built on the Greek noun for movement, so its plainest job is to mark anything that has to do with motion.
senses.whyCN: kinetic 就是由希腊语「运动」这一名词派生的形容词，因此最基本的作用是给一切与运动有关的事物作标记。

senses.title: Produced by movement
senses.definition: caused by or resulting from movement, often as heat or force
senses.definitionCN: 由移动引起的，常表现为热或力
senses.example: The friction of the brake pads turns kinetic energy into heat.
senses.exampleCN: 刹车片的摩擦把动能变成热。
senses.why: when a moving body is stopped, its motion does not vanish but appears as heat or wear, so the adjective also describes effects that motion produces.
senses.whyCN: 运动物体被拦住时，运动并未消失，而是以热或磨损的形式出现，因此这个词也描述运动所产生的结果。

senses.title: Of the energy carried by motion
senses.definition: describing the energy a body has because it is moving, as opposed to energy stored in its position
senses.definitionCN: 指物体因正在运动而具有的能量，与储存在位置中的能量相对
senses.example: A falling stone turns its kinetic energy into sound and heat on impact.
senses.exampleCN: 下落的石块在落地时把动能变成声与热。
senses.why: physics needed a short label for one quantity, the energy of motion, and fixed the pair kinetic energy against potential energy.
senses.whyCN: 物理学需要给一个量一个短标签，即运动的能量，于是固定下「动能」与「势能」这对说法。

senses.title: Explaining matter by moving particles
senses.titleCN: 用运动粒子解释物质性质
senses.definition: describing the model in which pressure, temperature and diffusion are explained by particles in constant motion
senses.definitionCN: 指用不断运动的粒子来解释压强、温度与扩散的模型
senses.example: The kinetic theory treats gas pressure as collisions of moving molecules.
senses.exampleCN: 分子运动论把气体压强看作运动分子碰撞的结果。
senses.why: once heat and pressure were traced to particles in motion, the adjective came to name the whole explanatory model, not just one body.
senses.whyCN: 一旦热与压强被归结为运动中的粒子，这个词就用来命名整套解释模型，而不只是单个物体。

senses.title: Art whose parts actually move
senses.definition: describing a work of art driven by motors, wind or water so that its parts move
senses.definitionCN: 指由马达、风或水驱动、部件真的会动的艺术品
senses.example: The gallery mounted a kinetic sculpture that turned with the draft.
senses.exampleCN: 美术馆展出了一件随气流转动的动态雕塑。
senses.why: twentieth-century artists borrowed the physics word to insist that the object itself moves, rather than merely showing movement.
senses.whyCN: 二十世纪艺术家借用了物理学的这个词，强调作品本身在动，而不只是描绘运动。

senses.title: Lively and quick
senses.definition: full of energy and quick in movement, used of people, music or an atmosphere
senses.definitionCN: 指人或音乐、气氛充满精力、动作轻快
senses.example: Her kinetic stage presence kept the audience awake.
senses.exampleCN: 她在台上那股灵动的气场让观众一直清醒。
senses.why: what moves fast reads as energetic, so the physical adjective slid easily into praise for liveliness.
senses.whyCN: 动得快的东西看上去就有劲，因此这个物理形容词很自然地滑向对「有活力」的称赞。

senses.title: Relating to human movement
senses.definition: relating to the analysis or therapy of the way the body moves
senses.definitionCN: 指对人体运动方式的分析或治疗
senses.example: The clinic uses kinetic analysis to correct a runner's stride.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所通过运动分析来纠正跑者的步态。
senses.why: medicine took the word for the mechanics of a moving body, especially when measuring gait and treating movement faults.
senses.whyCN: 医学借这个词指运动身体的力学，尤其在测量步态、治疗动作障碍时。

senses.title: Physical force in military use
senses.titleCN: 军事用语中的实体打击
senses.definition: describing a weapon or action that uses physical force rather than cyber or electronic means
senses.definitionCN: 指使用实体武力而非网络或电子手段的武器或行动
senses.example: Commanders weighed a kinetic response against a cyber one.
senses.exampleCN: 指挥官在实体打击与网络手段之间权衡。
senses.why: modern military writing divides actions into physical hits and non-physical ones, and calls the physical kind kinetic.
senses.whyCN: 现代军事写作把行动分为实体打击与非实体手段，并把实体那一类称为 kinetic。

intro.en: Kinetic comes from Greek kinētikos, an adjective meaning of or for moving, built on kinein, to move. It reached English through French in the nineteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: kinetic 来自希腊语形容词 kinētikos「关于运动的」，其词根为 kinein「移动」。这个词在 19 世纪经法语进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Kinein meant to move, to set in motion, to stir. Its deeper origin is not established; the Indo-European forms sometimes offered for it are reconstructions, not attested words.
items.cn: kinein 意为「移动、使动、搅动」。其更深来源未得到证明；有人为它给出的印欧语形式属于重构形式，并非有记录的词。

items.en: From kinētos, movable, plus the adjective ending -ikos, Greek formed kinētikos, of or for moving. The word described anything able to cause or receive motion.
items.cn: 由 kinētos「可动的」加形容词词尾 -ikos，希腊语构成 kinētikos「关于运动的」。这个词可形容一切能引起或接受运动的事物。

items.en: The same root gave kinēma, a movement, and kinēsis, the act of moving. These two nouns later supplied cinema and kinesis, which is why the family looks wider than the adjective alone.
items.cn: 同一词根还给出 kinēma「运动、移动之物」与 kinēsis「运动（行为）」。这两个名词后来提供了 cinema 与 kinesis，所以这个词族看起来比单个形容词更宽。

items.en: French cinétique, used by physicists in the 1830s, supplied the model for the English adjective; English kinetic is recorded from the 1840s.
items.cn: 法国物理学家在 1830 年代使用的 cinétique 为英语形容词提供了样板；英语 kinetic 自 1840 年代起有记录。

items.en: William Thomson and Peter Guthrie Tait fixed the phrase kinetic energy in the 1860s, setting it beside potential energy in the teaching of mechanics.
items.cn: 威廉·汤姆森与彼得·古思里·泰特在 1860 年代固定下 kinetic energy 这一说法，在力学的教学中把它与势能并置。

items.en: Source uncertain (pre-Greek origin): the earlier history of kinein is unsettled, and any single Indo-European root proposed for it is a reconstruction rather than a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: 来源不确定（希腊语之前的源头）：kinein 更早的历史没有定论，凡为它提出的单一印欧词根均属重构形式，而非已证实的派生。

note.en: The first group shares the Greek root for movement; the second group names neighbouring ideas of motion and energy with different emphasis.
note.cn: 第一组共享希腊语「运动」词根；第二组是意思相邻的「运动、能量」说法，侧重点各不相同。

entries.definition: The branch of mechanics that studies motion and the forces producing it; the noun looks like the plural of kinetic but names a science.
entries.definitionCN: 研究运动及产生运动的力的力学分支；形似 kinetic 的复数，实际是一门学科名。

entries.definition: Built on kinēma, a movement, and describing motion without asking what forces cause it, whereas kinetic belongs to the study of forces and energy.
entries.definitionCN: 由 kinēma「运动」构成，描述运动而不问其成因；kinetic 则属于力与能量的研究。

entries.definition: The Greek noun for movement; in biology it names a movement response of an organism to a stimulus.
entries.definitionCN: 希腊语「运动」这一名词；在生物学中指生物对刺激作出的运动反应。

entries.definition: Shortened from cinematograph, which was built on kinēma, a movement: pictures that move.
entries.definitionCN: 由 cinematograph 缩略而来，后者由 kinēma「运动」构成，意即「会动的画面」。

entries.definition: From Greek dynamis, power: it stresses force and energy, and in physics it belongs to the study of forces rather than of motion alone.
entries.definitionCN: 出自希腊语 dynamis「力量」：强调力与能量，在物理中属于力的研究，而不只是运动。

entries.definition: The everyday participle saying that something is in motion; kinetic is its technical and abstract counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 日常分词，直接说某物正在移动；kinetic 是它技术化、抽象化的对应词。

entries.definition: Able to move or be moved, said of phones, people and machinery; it describes capacity, not energy.
entries.definitionCN: 指能够移动或可被移动，用于电话、人与机械；说的是能力，不是能量。

entries.definition: Relating to machines and their parts; it overlaps with kinetic in mechanics but says nothing about motion itself.
entries.definitionCN: 与机器及其部件有关的；在力学中与 kinetic 有交集，但并不直接说「运动」。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Greek root, the real word family and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊词根、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Kinein is Greek for to move, so kinetic means having to do with movement.
normal.cn: kinein 是希腊语「移动」，所以 kinetic 就是「与运动有关」。

normal.en: The family runs kinetic, kinetics, kinetically, kinematic, kinesis and kinesiology.
normal.cn: 同族词有 kinetic、kinetics、kinetically、kinematic、kinesis 与 kinesiology。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the physical sense: kinetic energy, kinetic theory, kinetic friction.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出物理义：动能、分子运动论、动摩擦。

normal.en: The same root hides inside cinema, because early films were pictures that move.
normal.cn: 同一词根藏在 cinema 里，因为早期电影就是「会动的画面」。

normal.en: Energy of motion sits opposite energy of position, so kinetic energy and potential energy are learned as a pair.
normal.cn: 运动的能量与位置的能量相对，因此动能与势能总是成对学习。

abstract.en: Picture a struck bell whose rim is still trembling after the hammer is gone.
abstract.cn: 想象一口被敲过的钟，锤子已经离开，钟沿还在颤。

abstract.en: Picture a relay racer who has already stopped but hands the baton to legs still running.
abstract.cn: 想象一位已经停下的接力手，把接力棒交给还在跑的腿。

abstract.en: Picture a mobile hanging over a cot, turning because the room itself is breathing.
abstract.cn: 想象婴儿床上方悬挂的风铃，因为房间本身在呼吸而转动。

examples.en: Kinetic energy is passed from one billiard ball to the next on contact.
examples.cn: 动能就在两球相触时从一颗台球传到另一颗。

examples.en: The kinetic theory explains gas pressure without naming any single molecule.
examples.cn: 分子运动论解释气体压强，却不需要指名任何单个分子。

examples.en: A kinetic installation in the hall turned slowly with the ventilation draft.
examples.cn: 大厅里一件动态装置随着通风气流缓慢转动。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「开（ki）了引擎（netic）」——引擎一开，车就动起来 → 运动的、动能的

root: 希腊 kinein「移动」→ kinētikos「关于运动的」→ 法语 cinétique → 英语 kinetic；更早的印欧词根无定论，相关形式均属重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one gesture: something is moving, and the word tracks that motion into energy, into particles, into art, into a lively body and finally into physical force.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：某物在动，这个词便沿着运动追到能量、粒子、艺术、有活力的身体，最后追到实体武力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cue ball set in motion by a strike, passing its motion to another ball on contact.
core.cn: 核心意象：被球杆击中的母球带着运动前进，在相触的一瞬把运动传给另一颗球。

branches.en: PLAIN MOTION: whatever the subject, the adjective first says that motion is involved.
branches.cn: 单纯的运动：无论修饰什么，这个词首先说明与运动有关。

branches.en: ENERGY OF MOVEMENT: motion can be handed on or turned into heat, and physics gives it a fixed name.
branches.cn: 运动的能量：运动可以传递或变成热，物理学因此给它一个固定名称。

branches.en: PARTICLES: the adjective explains pressure and temperature by particles that never stop moving.
branches.cn: 粒子：这个词用永不停歇的粒子来解释压强与温度。

branches.en: MOTION SEEN OR MEASURED: art makes parts turn visibly, medicine measures how a body actually moves.
branches.cn: 被看见或被测量的运动：艺术让部件明显地转动，医学则测量身体实际的活动方式。

branches.en: INTENSITY: liveliness and physical force are both motion raised to a high pitch.
branches.cn: 强度：有活力与实体武力都是被推到高位的运动。

intro.en: Kinetic is Greek from start to finish: a verb root, two noun forms and an adjective ending. Latin supplied only the shape of the adjective ending.
intro.cn: kinetic 从头到尾都是希腊语：一个动词词根、两个名词形式与一个形容词词尾。拉丁语只提供了形容词词尾的形式。

latinIntro.en: No Latin noun stands behind this word, so the Latin entry list is empty; the ending -icus is the Latinised form of Greek -ikos.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词背后没有拉丁名词，因此拉丁词条列表留空；词尾 -icus 只是希腊语 -ikos 的拉丁化写法。

items.example: The root carries the bare act of moving.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根带着「移动」这个最单纯的动作。

items.example: Biology borrowed this noun for stimulus-driven movement.
items.exampleCN: 生物学借这个名词指由刺激驱动的运动。

items.example: Films were named from this noun because the pictures move.
items.exampleCN: 电影由这个名词得名，因为画面在动。

items.example: The adjective entered physics through French.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词经法语进入物理学。

items.example: The ending turns a noun of movement into a describing word.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把「运动」的名词变成描述性的词。

items.example: Kinetic energy is the energy of a moving body.
items.exampleCN: 动能就是运动物体具有的能量。

items.meaning: the study of motion and its causes
items.meaningCN: 研究运动及其成因的学科
items.example: Kinetics asks how fast a reaction proceeds.
items.exampleCN: 动力学研究反应进行得有多快。

items.meaningCN: 从运动角度；在运动方面
items.example: The two states differ kinetically, not in shape.
items.exampleCN: 这两种状态在运动方面不同，而非形状不同。

items.meaning: describing motion without regard to force
items.meaningCN: 描述运动而不论其力的
items.example: A kinematic model ignores what pushes the parts.
items.exampleCN: 运动学模型不考虑是什么推动这些部件。

items.example: Kinesiology maps how joints move under load.
items.exampleCN: 运动机能学描绘关节在受力时如何活动。

definition_zh: v. 使积满污垢；弄脏（尤指长期积累的烟垢油污）；（喻）使蒙污、败坏名声
definition_en: to cover with ingrained dirt, especially accumulated soot or grease; figuratively, to soil a reputation
core_image: 矿工升井时那张只剩眼白与牙齿还亮着的脸
scene: 矿工上来时，只有眼白和牙齿还是亮的。 The miners came up with faces begrimed, only the eyes and teeth still bright.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：begrimed 指被污垢覆满；句意是矿工升井时满脸积垢，只有眼睛与牙齿还亮。

senses.title: To coat with dirt
senses.definition: to make something dirty with grime that has built up over time
senses.definitionCN: 使某物覆上长期积累的污垢
senses.example: Years of coal smoke had begrimed the stone.
senses.exampleCN: 多年的煤烟把石头熏得发黑。
senses.why: The prefix be- means all over, so the verb describes a covering rather than a single mark.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 be- 意为「遍覆」，因此该动词描写的是覆盖，而非单个污点。

senses.title: To soil a reputation
senses.definition: figuratively, to blacken a name or record as if with soot
senses.definitionCN: 比喻义，指像被煤烟熏黑一样使名声或记录蒙污
senses.example: The scandal begrimed an otherwise clean record.
senses.exampleCN: 那桩丑闻给本来清白的记录抹了黑。
senses.why: Dirt on the surface becomes dirt on the character, a transfer English makes very readily.
senses.whyCN: 表面的脏转为品格的脏，这是英语极为顺手的一种引申。

intro.en: Begrime is the covering prefix be- plus grime, a Low Countries word for soot. The participle begrimed is far more common than the bare verb.
intro.cn: begrime 是「遍覆」前缀 be- 加 grime——一个来自低地国家的「煤烟」词。分词 begrimed 远比动词原形常用。

items.en: Old English be- could cover something all over, as in besmear and bedaub.
items.cn: 古英语 be- 可表「遍覆其上」，如 besmear、bedaub。

items.en: A Germanic root meant to smear or to rub in, the base of grime.
items.cn: 一个日耳曼语词根意为涂抹、擦入，是 grime 的基础。

items.en: Middle Dutch grime means soot or smut, and English takes it in about 1500.
items.cn: 中古荷兰语 grime 意为煤灰、烟垢，英语约 1500 年借入。

items.en: English adds the covering prefix to make a verb meaning to coat with dirt.
items.cn: 英语加上「遍覆」前缀造出该动词，意为覆满污垢。

items.en: Writers extend the word to reputations blackened by scandal.
items.cn: 文人把该词扩用于被丑闻涂黑的名声。

items.en: The participle becomes the commonest form, describing coal towns and faces.
items.cn: 分词形式成为最常用形式，用来描写煤城与面孔。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps other be- verbs so the prefix pattern becomes visible; the near-meaning group grades soiling from physical to moral.
note.cn: 形近组保留其他 be- 动词，使前缀规律显形；近义组把「弄脏」由物理到道德分级排列。

entries.definition: To charm or trick someone pleasantly.
entries.definitionCN: 以魅力诱骗或迷住某人。

entries.definition: To resent someone having something.
entries.definitionCN: 对他人的所得心生不甘。

entries.definition: To smear all over with something greasy.
entries.definitionCN: 把油腻之物涂满其上。

entries.definition: Dirt ingrained on a surface.
entries.definitionCN: 嵌入表面的污垢。

entries.definition: To make something dirty.
entries.definitionCN: 把东西弄脏。

entries.definition: To dirty, especially a reputation.
entries.definitionCN: 弄脏，尤指名声。

entries.definition: To make black, literally or morally.
entries.definitionCN: 使变黑，字面或道德义。

entries.definition: To spoil the purity of something.
entries.definitionCN: 败坏某物的清白。

normalIntro.en: Be- means all over, grime means soot: begrime is to put soot all over something. Learn the participle first.
normalIntro.cn: be- 意为「遍覆」，grime 意为「煤烟」：begrime 就是把煤烟覆满某物。先记分词形式。

normal.en: Grime is the dirt that will not wash off easily.
normal.cn: grime 是不易洗掉的积垢。

normal.en: Be- spreads it over the whole surface.
normal.cn: be- 把它铺满整个表面。

normal.en: Begrimed faces come up from the pit.
normal.cn: begrimed 的面孔从矿井里升上来。

normal.en: Compare besmear and bedaub, same prefix.
normal.cn: 对照 besmear、bedaub，同一前缀。

normal.en: A begrimed record is a moral use.
normal.cn: a begrimed record 是道德层面的用法。

abstract.en: Dirt that has been given time to settle.
abstract.cn: 被给予了时间沉落下来的脏。

abstract.en: A surface that records its own history.
abstract.cn: 一个记录着自身历史的表面。

abstract.en: Soot as evidence of work done.
abstract.cn: 煤烟作为劳作过的证据。

examples.en: The engine was begrimed with old oil.
examples.cn: 发动机上积满了陈年油污。

examples.en: Begrimed windows let in almost no light.
examples.cn: 积垢的窗几乎透不进光。

examples.en: Nothing could begrime his standing in the town.
examples.cn: 什么也败坏不了他在镇上的声望。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：be-「遍覆」+ grime「煤烟积垢」= begrime 弄得到处是垢。最常见的是分词 begrimed（begrimed with soot）。同类前缀：besmear、bedaub、begrudge。

root: 由前缀 be-「遍覆、彻底」加名词 grime 构成；grime 约 1500 年从中古荷兰语 grime「煤灰、烟垢」借入，深层日耳曼语词根意为涂抹。begrime 约 1530 年代出现，17 世纪扩出败坏名声的比喻义，实际使用中分词 begrimed 最常见。

sensesIntro.en: Two senses, one layer: soot settled on stone, and scandal settled on a name.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项，一层覆盖：落在石头上的煤烟，与落在名声上的丑闻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a miner face where only eyes and teeth are still bright
core.cn: 核心意象：矿工脸上只有眼白与牙齿还亮着

branches.en: A pit cage rising at dawn.
branches.cn: 黎明升起的矿井吊笼。

branches.en: Stone blackened under the paint.
branches.cn: 漆下被熏黑的石头。

branches.en: A headline over a clean record.
branches.cn: 清白记录之上的一条标题。

branches.en: A name that will not come clean.
branches.cn: 再也洗不白的名字。

branches.en: A layer time has pressed in.
branches.cn: 被时间压实的一层。

intro.en: The key part is the prefix be-, which turns a noun into a verb of covering; the rest build the adjective and moral synonyms.
intro.cn: 关键构件是前缀 be-，它把名词变成「覆盖」义动词；其余部分构成形容词与道德层面的近义词。

latinIntro.en: Latin sordidus means dirty, denigrare to blacken, and fuligo soot; denigrate is the learned twin of the figurative sense.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sordidus 意为脏，denigrare 意为抹黑，fuligo 意为煤烟；denigrate 是比喻义的书面孪生词。

definition_zh: 差异；不一致；出入；账目差额
definition_en: a difference between two things that ought to match
core_image: 两本账簿摊在同一张桌上，同一笔支出在两边写着不同的数字
scene: 两本账簿摊在同一张桌上，同一笔支出在两边写着不同的数字。 Auditors found a discrepancy between the two ledgers.
sceneCN: 这里指本应一致的两份记录出现差异（第 1 个义项：差异、不一致）；句意为审计人员发现两本账簿之间有出入。图中可辨识物件：账簿、两支笔、计算器、放大镜。

pos.zh: 名词：差异；不一致；出入（可数）

collocations.phrase: a discrepancy between the two accounts

collocations.zh: 理论与实践之间的不一致

senses.title: A difference between things that should match
senses.titleCN: 本应相符之物出现差异
senses.definition: a difference between two facts, figures or accounts that are expected to agree
senses.definitionCN: 本应一致的两项事实、数字或记录之间出现的差别
senses.example: Auditors found a discrepancy between the two ledgers.
senses.exampleCN: 审计人员发现两本账簿之间有出入。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to sound discordantly, so a discrepancy is two records refusing to sound alike.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「响声不谐」，因此差异就是两份记录的声音对不上。

senses.title: An accounting difference
senses.definition: a difference in a bookkeeping entry that prevents the books from balancing
senses.definitionCN: 使账目不平的一处记账差别
senses.example: A discrepancy of two hundred units delayed the audit.
senses.exampleCN: 一笔两百单位的差额拖慢了审计。
senses.why: A ledger is a set of figures that must agree, and any figure that does not add up is flagged by this word.
senses.whyCN: 账簿是一组必须对上的数字，任何加不平的数字都用这个词标出。

senses.title: A measurement difference
senses.definition: a difference between two measurements of the same quantity
senses.definitionCN: 同一数量两次测量之间出现的差别
senses.example: The discrepancy between the two instruments pointed to a loose sensor.
senses.exampleCN: 两台仪器之间的测量差异指向一个松动的传感器。
senses.why: Two instruments aimed at one quantity should read alike, so their disagreement is itself evidence.
senses.whyCN: 两台仪器测同一个量本应读数相同，因此它们的不一致本身就是证据。

senses.title: A gap between theory and data
senses.definition: a difference between what a model predicts and what is observed
senses.definitionCN: 模型预测与观测结果之间的差别
senses.example: The discrepancy between prediction and observation forced a revision.
senses.exampleCN: 预测与观测之间的差距迫使研究修改。
senses.why: Science advances when a model's promise and nature's answer fail to agree.
senses.whyCN: 当模型的承诺与自然的回答对不上时，科学才向前走。

senses.title: A gap between promise and practice
senses.definition: a difference between what is announced and what is actually done
senses.definitionCN: 宣布的内容与实际所做之事之间的差别
senses.example: The discrepancy between the policy and its enforcement was obvious.
senses.exampleCN: 政策与其执行之间的不一致一目了然。
senses.why: Words and deeds are two records of the same intention, and the word reports that they do not match.
senses.whyCN: 言辞与行动是同一个意图的两份记录，这个词报告两者对不上。

senses.title: An audit or statistical discrepancy
senses.definition: a mismatch uncovered by checking records against one another or against counts
senses.definitionCN: 把记录互相核对或与清点结果核对时发现的不符
senses.example: The census reported a discrepancy in two districts.
senses.exampleCN: 人口普查报告了两个辖区的一处出入。
senses.why: Counting twice is the oldest audit, and any gap between the two counts needs a name.
senses.whyCN: 数两遍是最古老的审计，两次清点之间的缺口需要一个名称。

senses.title: A difference between accounts of an event
senses.definition: a difference between two people's versions of the same event
senses.definitionCN: 两人对同一事件的叙述之间出现的差别
senses.example: The discrepancy between the two witnesses puzzled the court.
senses.exampleCN: 两名证人陈述之间的差异让法庭困惑。
senses.why: Two observers of one event should tell one story, and their divergence is what courts must resolve.
senses.whyCN: 同一件事的两名观察者本应讲出一个版本，他们的分歧正是法庭要解决的。

senses.title: A discrepancy in replication
senses.definition: a failure of a second experiment to reproduce the first result
senses.definitionCN: 第二次实验未能再现第一次结果
senses.example: The discrepancy between the two trials raised doubts about the finding.
senses.exampleCN: 两次试验之间的不一致使人们对结论产生怀疑。
senses.why: Replication is a second record of the same effect, and a mismatch weakens the first claim.
senses.whyCN: 重复实验是同一效应的第二份记录，对不上就削弱了第一个结论。

intro.en: Discrepancy comes from Latin discrepantia, discordance, from discrepare, to sound discordantly, built from dis-, apart, and crepare, to rattle or creak. English took the noun in the seventeenth century.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语 discrepantia「不和谐」，源头是动词 discrepare「响声不和」，由表示「分开」的前缀与表示「嘎嘎作响」的词根构成。英语在十七世纪借入这个名词。

items.en: The verb meant to rattle, creak or make a noise, and it also stands behind decrepit.
items.cn: 这个动词意为嘎嘎作响、吱嘎出声，也是「破旧」一词的源头。

items.en: The prefix meant apart or in different directions.
items.cn: 这个前缀意为分开、朝不同方向。

items.en: The compound meant to sound out of tune with one another.
items.cn: 这个复合动词意为彼此的声音不合调。

items.en: The noun named the state of not agreeing, first of sounds and then of facts.
items.cn: 这个名词指不一致的状态，先用于声音，后用于事实。

items.en: French carried the noun into English, where it named mismatches in records and accounts.
items.cn: 法语把这个名词带进英语，用于指记录与账目中的不符。

items.en: Later usage extended it to measurements, statistics, testimony and replication.
items.cn: 后来的用法把它扩展到测量、统计、证词与重复实验。

note.en: The first group shares the root or the noun ending; the second group names other kinds of difference.
note.cn: 第一组共享词根或名词词尾；第二组是其他表示差异的说法。

entries.definition: The adjective for things that do not agree.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，指不一致的。

entries.definition: In a manner that does not agree.
entries.definitionCN: 指以不一致的方式。

entries.definition: Separate and distinct; close in spelling but from another Latin verb.
entries.definitionCN: 分开而独立；拼写相近，但来自另一个拉丁动词。

entries.definition: Careful judgement or freedom to decide; a different Latin verb behind it.
entries.definitionCN: 谨慎判断或自行决定的自由；背后是另一个拉丁动词。

entries.definition: Worn out, from the same verb of creaking.
entries.definitionCN: 指破旧的，出自同一个「吱嘎作响」动词。

entries.definition: The general word for two things not being the same.
entries.definitionCN: 指两物不相同的一般说法。

entries.definition: A failure to stay the same from one case to the next.
entries.definitionCN: 指前后未能保持一致。

entries.definition: A difference in level or condition, often unfair.
entries.definitionCN: 指水平或状况上的差距，常带不公平意味。

entries.definition: A change or difference within a range.
entries.definitionCN: 指范围内出现的变化或差异。

entries.definition: An empty space or a shortfall between two points.
entries.definitionCN: 指空缺或两点之间的落差。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations follow the Latin image of sounds that will not agree, then apply it to books, instruments and testimony.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想沿着拉丁语中「声音合不到一起」的意象，再把它用到账簿、仪器与证词上。

normal.en: The root verb means to creak, so a discrepancy is two records creaking out of tune.
normal.cn: 词根意为嘎嘎作响，所以差异就是两份记录的响声不合调。

normal.en: Auditors look for a discrepancy between the ledger and the count.
normal.cn: 审计人员找的是账簿与清点结果之间的出入。

normal.en: Two instruments measuring the same thing should agree, and their discrepancy points to a fault.
normal.cn: 两台仪器测同一件事本应一致，它们的差异指向某个故障。

normal.en: A model that predicts one value while observation gives another has a discrepancy to explain.
normal.cn: 模型预测一个值、观测给出另一个值，就有差异需要解释。

normal.en: Two witnesses telling different stories create a discrepancy for the court.
normal.cn: 两名证人讲出不同版本，就给法庭造成一处不一致。

abstract.en: A discrepancy is a place where two truths refuse to sit on the same line.
abstract.cn: 差异是两个真相不肯坐进同一条线的地方。

abstract.en: Records are promises to agree, and the word reports a broken promise.
abstract.cn: 记录是「应当一致」的承诺，这个词报告承诺被违背。

abstract.en: What cannot be made to agree can still be made to explain, which is where research begins.
abstract.cn: 无法被凑成一致的东西仍可被解释，研究就从这里开始。

examples.en: The discrepancy between the invoice and the order delayed payment.
examples.cn: 发票与订单之间的出入拖慢了付款。

examples.en: A discrepancy in the two measurements suggested a faulty gauge.
examples.cn: 两次测量间的差异表明仪表有故障。

examples.en: The committee asked the agency to explain the discrepancy in its figures.
examples.cn: 委员会要求该机构解释数字上的出入。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「迪斯克瑞彭西」——两本账对不上，嘎嘎响不到一个调上，就是「差异、不一致」：差异、出入

root: 来自拉丁语 discrepantia「不和谐」，源头 discrepare「响声不和」，由 dis-「分开」与 crepare「嘎嘎作响」构成；英语在十七世纪借入，后扩展到测量、统计、证词与重复实验。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses trace a mismatch through records, accounts, instruments, models, promises, audits, testimony and replication.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把「对不上」追到记录、账目、仪器、模型、承诺、审计、证词与重复实验。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two ledgers open on one desk, the same expense written in two different figures.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一张桌上两本摊开的账簿，同一笔支出写着两个不同数字。

branches.en: THE TWO VERSIONS: records and testimony fail to agree on one event.
branches.cn: 两个版本：记录与证词在同一件事上对不上。

branches.en: THE BOOKS AND THE COUNT: an audit finds figures that will not balance.
branches.cn: 账簿与清点：审计发现数字无法轧平。

branches.en: THE INSTRUMENTS DISAGREE: two measurements of one quantity differ.
branches.cn: 仪器不一致：同一数量的两次测量出现差别。

branches.en: THE PREDICTION AND THE REPEAT: a model misses the data, and a second trial misses the first.
branches.cn: 预测与重复：模型对不上数据，第二次试验对不上第一次。

branches.en: THE PROMISE AND THE PRACTICE: what is announced is not what is done.
branches.cn: 承诺与做法：宣布的内容并非实际所做。

intro.en: The word is built on a Latin verb of harsh sound, so its core image is two things out of tune.
intro.cn: 这个词建在表示「刺耳声响」的拉丁动词上，核心意象是两样东西不合调。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies the verb of creaking, the prefix of separation, the compound verb and the noun of discord.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了表示吱嘎作响的动词、表示分开的前缀、复合动词与表示不谐的名词。

items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供声响意象。

items.example: The adjective adds a Latin ending.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词加了拉丁词尾。

items.exampleCN: 它标记类似分词的形容词。

It forms the adverb.

items.exampleCN: 出自同一个「吱嘎」动词的相关词。

definition_zh: 使（帆船）因无风而停滞；使平静
definition_en: to leave a sailing ship unable to move because there is no wind, or to make calm
core_image: 帆布瘫软，船身纹丝不动地钉在海面
scene: 连日无风，帆船在烈日下停在海中央。 The fleet was becalmed for a week under a cloudless sky.
sceneCN: 这里 becalmed 是「因无风而停滞」（第 1 个义项：帆船因无风无法航行）；句意是船队在无云的晴空下停滞了一周。

derivatives.zh: 由过去分词转形容词，义为「因无风而停滞的」
由 calm 加 -ness 构成，义为「平静；镇静」

senses.title: To strand a ship without wind
senses.definition: to leave a sailing ship motionless because the wind has dropped
senses.definitionCN: 因风力消失使帆船动弹不得
senses.example: The fleet was becalmed for a week under a cloudless sky.
senses.exampleCN: 船队在无云的晴空下停滞了一周。
senses.why: The prefix be- acts on the object, so becalm means to make a ship calm, that is windless and stuck.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 be- 作用于宾语，becalm 即「使船平静」，也就是无风受困。

senses.title: To make calm
senses.definition: to make someone or something calm and still
senses.definitionCN: 使某人或某物平静安定
senses.example: The slow lapping of the tide seemed to becalm the anxious traveller.
senses.exampleCN: 潮水轻缓的拍岸声似乎让焦虑的旅人平静下来。
senses.why: From making a ship still, the verb widened to stilling minds and weather.
senses.whyCN: 由「使船静止」扩展到安抚心绪与天气。

intro.en: Becalm joins the prefix be- with calm.
intro.cn: becalm 由前缀 be- 加 calm 构成。

items.en: be- comes from Old English be-, about, around, thoroughly.
items.cn: 前缀 be- 来自古英语，表示「围绕、彻底」。

items.en: calm came through Italian calma from Greek kauma, heat of the day.
items.cn: calm 经意大利语 calma，源自希腊语 kauma「正午暑热」。

items.en: becalm appeared in nautical use for windless stranding.
items.cn: 十六世纪 becalm 用于航海语境，指无风受困。

items.en: the verb widened to calming minds and weather.
items.cn: 后来动词义扩展至安抚心绪与天气。

items.en: becalmed is now common as an adjective for stranded ships and stilled places.
items.cn: 如今 becalmed 常作形容词，形容停滞的船只与静止的地方。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the be- prefix; the near-meaning group gathers words for windless stillness and calming.
note.cn: 形近组共享 be- 前缀；近义组汇集无风静止与安抚之词。

entries.definition: to decorate

entries.definition: motionless for lack of wind
entries.definitionCN: 停滞无风的——becalm 的分词形式

normalIntro.cn: becalm 在 calm 前加 be-：使船「平静」——也就是走不了。

normal.en: The be- prefix acts on an object.
normal.cn: be- 前缀作用于宾语。

normal.en: A becalmed ship has no wind.
normal.cn: becalmed 的船无风可借。

normal.en: The past forms are becalmed.
normal.cn: 过去式与过去分词是 becalmed。

normal.cn: becalmed 也可形容静下来的心。

normal.en: Compare befog and bedeck, same pattern.

abstract.en: See sails hanging limp in dead air.
abstract.cn: 想象帆布在死寂的空气里瘫软。

abstract.en: Feel days pass with the horizon unmoving.
abstract.cn: 感受地平线纹丝不动的漫长日子。

abstract.en: Picture worry settling like flat water.
abstract.cn: 想象忧虑如平水般沉降。

examples.en: A becalmed sailing ship drifts wherever the current wants.
examples.cn: 无风停滞的帆船随洋流漂向何处全凭它意。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「比·咖姆」——大家比赛喝咖啡摸鱼，因为船无风停航，闲得只能喝咖啡。

sensesIntro.cn: 一个动词，先停住无风的船，再抚平不宁的心。
